DEA-C01 is current (no successor found) · 65 Q (50 scored + 15 unscored) · MC (1 of 4) + multiple-response (2+ of 5+) · 130 min · pass **720/1000** (scaled, compensatory) · USD 150 · EN/JA/KO/ZH · Pearson VUE centre or online · valid 3 y · retake after 14 days · ESL +30 min available.

# 00 — Exam overview (DEA-C01, exam guide v1.1) — last verified 2026-10-20
Sources: exam guide + cert page + policy pages (see `docs/sources.md`). Everything below marked ✓ was read on the official pages today.

## Facts ✓
- **DEA-C01 is the current exam**; no successor or retirement notice found. Guide v1.1 published 2025-12-12 (effective ~1 month later); new guide versions are published ≥ 1 month before they affect the exam.
- 65 questions = 50 scored + 15 unscored (unidentified); multiple choice (1 of 4) and multiple response (2+ of 5+); no penalty for guessing; unanswered = wrong.
- 130 minutes · scaled 100–1000 · **pass 720** · pass/fail · compensatory (no per-domain minimum) · USD 150 · languages EN/JA/KO/ZH-Simplified (can toggle to English) · Pearson VUE test centre or online proctored · valid 3 years · retake after 14 days (unlimited attempts, full fee) · ESL +30 min accommodation available.
- Target candidate: 2–3 years data engineering, 1–2 years AWS. Out of scope: ML training/inference, language-specific syntax, business conclusions.

"Amazon Quick" and "Kinesis Data Firehose" appear under those names in the guide (Quick = QuickSight family; Firehose = Amazon Data Firehose).

# Task 1.1 — Perform data ingestion (Domain 1 = 34 % of scored content)
Tags: ✓ verified 2026-10-20 against the linked AWS page · ~ established, not re-fetched · [UNVERIFIED] see `docs/open-questions.md`. Skills covered: 1.1.1–1.1.12 (exam guide v1.1).

## 0. Skill → section map
| Skill | Section | Skill | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.1.1 streaming sources | §1–§4 | 1.1.7 Lambda from Kinesis | §3 |
| 1.1.2 batch sources | §5 | 1.1.8 IP allowlists | §8 |
| 1.1.3 batch config | §5 | 1.1.9 throttling | §9 |
| 1.1.4 data APIs | §6 | 1.1.10 fan-in / fan-out | §10 |
| 1.1.5 schedulers | §7 | 1.1.11 replayability | §11 |
| 1.1.6 event triggers | §7 | 1.1.12 stateful vs stateless | §12 |

## 1. Streaming ingestion — the service-selection core
**Concept (3 lines).** Streaming services differ on four axes: *replay*, *consumer model*, *latency*, *operations*. Pick by the axis the stem emphasises. Words like "replay", "multiple independent consumers", "ordering per key" point to a log (KDS/MSK); "load into S3/Redshift with no code" points to Firehose; "decouple/retry/DLQ" points to SQS; "fan-out" to SNS; "route events by content/schedule" to EventBridge.

| | Kinesis Data Streams | Amazon Data Firehose | MSK | SQS | SNS | EventBridge |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Model | ordered log (shards) | delivery pipeline | Kafka log (partitions) | queue | pub/sub | event bus + rules |
| Replay | ✓ 24 h–365 d | ✗ | ✓ (retention set by you; Serverless unlimited ✓) | ✗ | ✗ | archive/replay feature ~ |
| Consumers | many; shared 2 MB/s/shard or EFO | none (destinations) | many consumer groups | competing | many subscribers | many targets |
| Ordering | per partition key | n/a | per partition | FIFO + MessageGroupId | FIFO topics ~ | no guarantee |
| Latency | ~100 ms; EFO ~70 ms ~ | ≥ 60 s buffer (60–900 s) ✓ | ms | ms | ms | ~sec |
| Ops | shards or on-demand | none | cluster or serverless | none | none | none |
When NOT: KDS for simple "land in S3" (use Firehose, cheaper in ops); Firehose when you need replay/ordering/custom consumers; MSK when you have no Kafka requirement (KDS is simpler); SQS when you need replay or multiple consumers of the same message.

## 2. Kinesis Data Streams (KDS)
Source: [KDS quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/service-sizes-and-limits.html) ✓
- **Provisioned shard**: write **1 MB/s or 1,000 records/s**; read **2 MB/s or 2,000 records/s** shared across classic consumers; **5 GetRecords calls/s/shard**; each call ≤ 10 MB / 10,000 records. **Record payload ≤ 10 MiB** (burst capacity for 1–10 MiB records). PutRecords ≤ 500 records / 10 MiB.
- **On-demand**: starts at 4 MB/s write / 8 MB/s read; scales to 10 GB/s w / 20 GB/s r in us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1 (200/400 MB/s other Regions); 50 on-demand streams default; mode switch twice per 24 h. Provisioned: 20,000 shards/account in the three big Regions, 1,000 or 6,000 elsewhere.
- **Retention** 24 h (default) → 365 d. **EFO consumers**: 20 per stream (50 with On-demand Advantage). Shard iterator valid 5 min. Merge/split shards provisioned only.
- **Shard math** (memorise): shards = max( ⌈MB/s ÷ 1⌉, ⌈records/s ÷ 1,000⌉, ⌈consumer MB/s read ÷ 2⌉ ). Example: 6,000 rec/s × 500 B = 3 MB/s → bytes need 3 shards, records need **6** → 6 shards. Three classic consumers each reading all data of an 18 MB/s stream need 54 MB/s read > 2 MB/s × 18 shards = 36 → use **enhanced fan-out**.
- **Producers**: SDK (PutRecord/PutRecords), KPL (aggregation + batching, async), Kinesis Agent. **Consumers**: KCL (DynamoDB lease table, checkpointing, one worker per shard), Lambda, Managed Service for Apache Flink, Firehose.
- Hot shard: skewed partition key → higher-cardinality key or random suffix; `WriteProvisionedThroughputExceeded`. Lag: `GetRecords.IteratorAgeMilliseconds`.
- Security: SSE-KMS, TLS, interface VPC endpoint, IAM stream/consumer ARNs.

## 3. Calling Lambda from Kinesis (skill 1.1.7) ✓ [Lambda + Kinesis](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-kinesis.html)
- Lambda *polls* each shard (standard iterator ≈ once per second, shares the 2 MB/s) or receives pushed records over HTTP/2 from an **EFO** consumer. One batch per shard at a time; **in-order per shard; an error stops the shard** until the batch succeeds or expires (poison-pill).
- Batching: invokes as soon as records exist unless you set a **batching window up to 5 min**; stops at full batch or **6 MB** payload.
- **ParallelizationFactor 1–10** = concurrent batches per shard (ordering preserved per partition key) — the fix for rising IteratorAge with a fast function.
- Error handling knobs ~: BisectBatchOnFunctionError, MaximumRetryAttempts, MaximumRecordAgeInSeconds, on-failure destination (SQS/SNS/S3), tumbling windows for stateful aggregation.
- **At-least-once** → make the function **idempotent** (warned in docs ✓). Aggregated (KPL) records + EFO: records whose partition key doesn't match the aggregate key are **dropped** ✓ (edge-case, optional).
- Concurrency: reserve concurrency or request quota if the function can't keep up (shards × ParallelizationFactor concurrent batches).

## 4. Other streaming sources
**Amazon Data Firehose** (renamed from Kinesis Data Firehose) ✓ [Firehose quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/limits.html)
- Buffer interval 60–900 s; record ≤ 1,000 KiB; PutRecordBatch ≤ 500 records or 4 MiB; Direct PUT default 500,000 rec/s / 2,000 req/s / 5 MiB/s in us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1 (100,000 / 1,000 / 1 MiB elsewhere), auto-scales, no cap when the source is KDS. DirectPut retains 24 h if destination down.
- Features: Lambda transformation (5 concurrent invocations/shard), record format conversion JSON→Parquet/ORC using a Glue table ~, **dynamic partitioning** (500 active partitions/stream, 1 GB/s per partition), compression, backup of failed records to S3.
- Destinations: S3, Redshift (**publicly accessible clusters only** ✓), OpenSearch, Splunk, HTTP endpoint, Snowflake ~, Iceberg tables [UNVERIFIED]. Sources: Direct PUT, KDS, MSK ✓ (10 MB/s per partition; ≤ 6 MB records if Lambda enabled ✓), CloudWatch Logs/EventBridge etc. ~
- Pricing quirk ✓: ingestion billed per record rounded up to 5 KB → batch tiny records.
- Private Redshift + streaming? Use **Redshift streaming ingestion** (materialized view over KDS/MSK; concurrency scaling for KDS refresh ✓ P203 Aug 2026).

**Amazon MSK** ✓ [MSK quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/msk/latest/developerguide/limits.html)
- Standard brokers: ≤ 30 brokers/cluster (ZooKeeper) or 60 (KRaft), 90/account, 1 GiB–16 TiB storage per broker, 3,000 IAM-auth connections/broker. **Express brokers**: unlimited storage, per-partition max 15 MB/s, instance-based throughput caps.
- **MSK Serverless**: 200 MB/s in, 400 MB/s out per cluster; **5 MB/s in / 10 MB/s out per partition**; 2,400 partitions (non-compacted); max message **8 MiB**; unlimited retention; 3,000 connections; IAM auth; 10 clusters/account.
- MSK Connect (managed Kafka Connect): ≤ 10 workers per connector. MSK Replicator for cross-cluster/Region copies. MSK Data Delivery channels to S3/S3 Tables (5–15 min freshness) ✓.
- Choose MSK when: Kafka APIs/ecosystem (Streams, Connect, MirrorMaker), existing apps. Auth: IAM, SASL/SCRAM (Secrets Manager), mTLS ~.

**DynamoDB Streams** ~: ordered item changes, 24 h retention, ≤ 2 simultaneous readers/shard ✓ (1 for global tables). Alternative: **Kinesis Data Streams destination for DynamoDB** (longer retention, many consumers, then Firehose to S3). EventBridge Pipes connects Streams to targets with filter/enrich ✓.

**DMS CDC** ✓ [DMS S3 target](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Target.S3.html): modes full load, CDC, or both; targets include S3, Kinesis, Kafka/MSK, Redshift ~. S3 target writes **CSV by default, Parquet optional**; full-load files `LOAD00000001.csv…` and CDC files named by timestamp under `schema/table/`; control file size with `MaxFileSize`. Parallel full load / more subtasks speed large tables. CDC rows carry an operation column (I/U/D) ~.

**Glue streaming ETL** (Spark Structured Streaming micro-batches from KDS/Kafka, serverless; G.025X worker for small streams ✓) and **Redshift** (MV streaming ingestion) are also listed as streaming readers in skill 1.1.1.

## 5. Batch sources and configuration (1.1.2, 1.1.3)
| Source | How read | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| S3 | Glue/EMR/Athena/Redshift COPY/Lambda | prefix + partition pruning; avoid small files; S3 events for arrival |
| RDS/on-prem DB | Glue JDBC (partitioned read), DMS, zero-ETL (Aurora/RDS→Redshift ✓ ~) | read replica / snapshot export to protect OLTP |
| Redshift | UNLOAD to S3, Glue connector, data sharing | |
| SaaS | **AppFlow** (Salesforce, SAP, ServiceNow…; schedule/event/on-demand) | no code; zero-ETL for some SaaS ✓ (Glue docs) |
| Files from on-prem | **DataSync** (scheduled, verified, bandwidth-controlled), Transfer Family (SFTP/FTPS/FTP/AS2 endpoint), Snow Family (offline) | |
| EMR | Spark/Hive jobs reading HDFS/S3/EMRFS | |
**Batch configuration choices (1.1.3)**: incremental vs full (bookmarks, watermark columns, DMS CDC), file size/partitioning (128 MB–1 GB), parallel JDBC reads (partition column + bounds, `hashfield/hashpartitions`), retries/timeouts, schedule vs event, idempotent writes, compression, `fetchsize`, worker type/number, S3 `groupFiles/groupSize` for many small files.

## 6. Consuming data APIs (1.1.4)
Pull on a schedule from REST APIs: Glue Python shell/Lambda (≤15 min ✓) + EventBridge Scheduler; AppFlow for SaaS APIs. Handle **pagination**, **429/rate limits** (exponential backoff + jitter, SQS buffer with max concurrency), auth secrets in Secrets Manager, idempotent writes. Long (> 15 min) pulls → Glue Python shell or ECS/Fargate task via Step Functions.

## 7. Schedulers and event triggers (1.1.5, 1.1.6)
**EventBridge Scheduler** ✓ [Scheduler](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/scheduler/latest/UserGuide/what-is-scheduler.html): cron/rate/**one-time** schedules, **flexible time windows**, retry policy + max retention for failed triggers, **at-least-once** delivery, templated targets (SQS, SNS, Lambda, EventBridge) and **universal targets** (270+ services, 6,000+ API operations, e.g., start a Glue job/Step Functions directly). Time zone support ~ (scheduled *rules* are UTC-only ~).
Other: Glue triggers (scheduled/conditional/on-demand/EventBridge) and workflows; MWAA schedule_interval/sensors; time-based = cron on any of these.
**Event triggers**: S3 Event Notifications → Lambda, SQS, SNS, EventBridge ✓ (Glue job is *not* a direct destination → go via EventBridge/Lambda); EventBridge rules on AWS service events (Glue job state change, Step Functions). Pattern: S3 → EventBridge → Step Functions → crawler → job (event-driven, no polling).

## 8. IP allowlists (1.1.8)
Outbound fixed IP for sources that allow-list: **NAT gateway + Elastic IP** (private subnet jobs); give that EIP to the partner. Inbound control: security groups (stateful), NACLs (stateless), VPC endpoints/PrivateLink, S3 bucket policy `aws:SourceIp`/`aws:SourceVpce`. For Glue JDBC: connection with VPC/subnet/SG.

## 9. Throttling and rate limits (1.1.9)
| Target | Symptom | Pattern |
|---|---|---|
| DynamoDB | `ProvisionedThroughputExceededException` | on-demand or auto scaling; spread keys; batch writes; SDK retries with backoff |
| RDS | connection exhaustion / load | RDS Proxy, SQS buffer + limited Lambda max concurrency, read replica, bounded Glue parallelism |
| Kinesis | `Write/ReadProvisionedThroughputExceeded` | more shards/on-demand, better key, PutRecords/KPL, EFO |
| S3 | 503 Slow Down | > 3,500/5,500 req/s/prefix ✓ → prefixes, fewer files, backoff |
| Third-party API | 429 | SQS + max concurrency, Step Functions Map `MaxConcurrency`, Wait/Retry |
Universal answer shape: **buffer (SQS/Kinesis) + bound concurrency + exponential backoff with jitter + idempotency**.

## 10. Fan-in and fan-out (1.1.10)
Fan-in: many producers → one stream (partition keys, KPL, agents, IoT rules). Fan-out: KDS **EFO** ✓ (20/50 consumers), KDS → Firehose + Flink + Lambda in parallel, **SNS → SQS** per subscriber (independent retries, DLQ; filter policies), EventBridge rules with multiple targets, MSK consumer groups.

## 11. Replayability (1.1.11)
Design so any stage can be rerun: raw immutable zone in S3; stream retention (KDS ≤ 365 d ✓, MSK); idempotent loads (MERGE/upsert or stage-then-swap); deterministic transforms; reset Glue bookmarks; Iceberg snapshots/time travel; EventBridge archive; SQS cannot replay (use DLQ redrive). Firehose does not retain for replay (24 h buffer only when destination fails ✓).

## 12. Stateful vs stateless (1.1.12)
Stateless: per-record map/filter/parse (Lambda, Firehose transform). Stateful: needs memory across records — windows, dedupe, joins, sessionization — **Flink** (keyed state, checkpoints, exactly-once), Spark Structured Streaming, Lambda tumbling windows (small). State must be checkpointed; replays require idempotent sinks.

## 13. Worked scenarios
1. *18 MB/s stream, three independent consumers, bursty, least ops* → **KDS on-demand + enhanced fan-out** (shared reads would need 54 MB/s vs 36 MB/s available; provisioned adds planning).
2. *Private Redshift cluster, near-real-time from Kinesis, least code* → **Redshift streaming ingestion MV** (Firehose cannot target private clusters ✓).
3. *Partner drops a file at unknown time; run crawler then job once* → **S3 → EventBridge → Step Functions** (not hourly schedule, not polling).
4. *DB→S3 lake with ongoing changes, Parquet, no code* → **DMS full load + CDC to S3 (Parquet)**; for Aurora→Redshift use **zero-ETL**.

## 14. Snippets (untested)
```bash
# On-demand stream + enhanced fan-out consumer
aws kinesis create-stream --stream-name clicks --stream-mode-details StreamMode=ON_DEMAND
aws kinesis register-stream-consumer --stream-arn arn:aws:kinesis:us-east-1:123456789012:stream/clicks --consumer-name fraud

# Lambda event source mapping: robust Kinesis consumer
aws lambda create-event-source-mapping --function-name proc \
  --event-source-arn arn:aws:kinesis:us-east-1:123456789012:stream/clicks/consumer/fraud:1540591608 \
  --starting-position LATEST --batch-size 200 --maximum-batching-window-in-seconds 5 \
  --parallelization-factor 4 --bisect-batch-on-function-error --maximum-retry-attempts 3 \
  --destination-config '{"OnFailure":{"Destination":"arn:aws:sqs:us-east-1:123456789012:dlq"}}'
```

## 15. Keyword → answer and traps
| Keyword | Answer | Trap |
|---|---|---|
| replay, reprocess, many consumers | KDS / MSK | Firehose |
| near real time to S3, no code | Firehose | KDS + Lambda |
| existing Kafka | MSK | KDS |
| rising iterator age | ParallelizationFactor / EFO / shards | more memory |
| poison record blocks shard | bisect + retries + on-failure destination | more shards |
| Firehose → private Redshift | streaming ingestion MV | Firehose directly |
| fixed IP for partner allowlist | NAT + EIP | S3 gateway endpoint |
| DB CDC to lake | DMS (full load + CDC) | DataSync |
| SaaS ingest | AppFlow | custom Lambda |

# Task 1.2 — Transform and process data (D1)
Tags: ✓ verified 2026-10-20 (link) · ~ established, not re-fetched. Skills 1.2.1–1.2.10.

## 0. Skill → section map
1.2.1 containers §6 · 1.2.2 JDBC/ODBC §7 · 1.2.3 integrate sources §7 · 1.2.4 cost §8 · 1.2.5 pick engine §1–§5 · 1.2.6 formats §9 · 1.2.7 troubleshooting §10 · 1.2.8 data APIs §11 · 1.2.9 3 Vs §12 · 1.2.10 LLMs §13

## 1. Choosing the transformation engine (skill 1.2.5) — the most tested decision
| Engine | Best for | Not for | Ops | Cost model |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **AWS Glue** (Spark) | serverless ETL, catalog-integrated, bookmarks, DQ, many connectors | very custom frameworks (HBase, Presto tuning), sub-second streaming | lowest for Spark | DPU-hours (per-second, min duration ~) |
| **Glue Python shell** | small scripts, API pulls, light pandas (1/16 or 1 DPU ~) | big data | none | cheap |
| **EMR** (EC2 / EKS / Serverless) | custom Spark/Hive/Presto/HBase/Flink, tuning, Spot, existing Hadoop code | "least ops" asks (EC2) | EC2 high; Serverless low | EC2/Spot hours; Serverless vCPU/GB-hours |
| **Lambda** | event-driven small transforms ≤ 15 min ✓, ≤ 10,240 MB ✓ | big joins/long jobs | none | per-ms |
| **Athena** (CTAS/INSERT/UNLOAD) | SQL ELT on S3, format conversion, compaction | custom code (use Spark notebooks) | none | per TB scanned |
| **Redshift** | SQL ELT where data already is; heavy joins; MVs | unstructured raw | low–medium | node/RPU |
| **Managed Service for Apache Flink** | stateful real-time | batch | low | KPU-hours |
| **DataBrew** | no-code cleaning/profiling | complex logic | none | per node-hour/session |
| **AWS Batch / ECS / EKS** | containerised custom jobs, long-running | simple SQL | medium | compute |
Decision shortcuts: "serverless Spark + JDBC + schedule" → Glue. "Custom libraries, occasional Spark, no cluster" → **EMR Serverless**. "Existing EKS, share capacity" → **EMR on EKS**. "HBase/specific frameworks" → EMR on EC2. "Convert CSV→Parquet with SQL only" → Athena CTAS (or Glue). "Real-time windows" → Flink.

## 2. AWS Glue essentials ✓ [Glue job properties](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/add-job.html)
- **Versions** ✓: 6.0 (Spark 4.1.1, Python 3.13), **5.1 (Spark 3.5.6, Python 3.11; default for new jobs)**, 5.0, 4.0, 3.0. [Earlier cheatsheet note "5.1 current" → 6.0 now exists; exam-relevant fact is "newer versions give newer Spark/Python and open-table libraries".]
- **Job types**: Spark (`glueetl`), Spark Streaming (`gluestreaming`), Python shell (`pythonshell`).
- **Workers (DPU = 4 vCPU + 16 GB)** ✓: G.025X 0.25 DPU (streaming only, low volume) · **G.1X** 1 DPU (4 vCPU/16 GB) · **G.2X** 2 DPU (8/32) · G.4X 4 · G.8X 8 · G.12X 12 · G.16X 16; memory-optimised **R.1X–R.8X** for OOM-prone jobs (higher start latency). G.1X/G.2X cover most jobs.
- **Flex** ✓: flexible execution class for non-urgent jobs (Glue 3.0+, **G.1X/G.2X only**); billed per worker-time actually running; may start later. **Standard** for time-sensitive.
- **Timeout** ✓: configurable up to **7 days**; default 2,880 min (≤ Glue 4.0) or **480 min (5.0+)**; **retries 0–10**; timed-out jobs aren't retried. **Max concurrency** default 1 per job (error when exceeded) unless raised; **job run queuing** option waits for quota instead of failing.
- **Auto scaling** (Glue 3.0+ ~) adds/removes workers within max.
- **Bookmarks** ✓: remember processed data; need `transformation_ctx` + `job.commit()` ~. Not supported with LF **cell-level filters** ✓ (also push-down predicates, `enableUpdateCatalog`).
- Security configuration (KMS for S3 output, CloudWatch Logs, bookmarks) · Job metrics + observability metrics + continuous logging + Spark UI (set a Spark UI logs path) ✓ · "Use Glue Data Catalog as Hive metastore" option ✓ · Temporary path in S3 (used by Redshift reads/writes) ✓.
- **DynamicFrame** (schema-on-the-fly, `ResolveChoice`, `ApplyMapping`, `Relationalize` to flatten nested JSON) vs Spark DataFrame (fixed schema, richer API). Convert with `toDF()` / `fromDF()`.
- **Pushdown predicate** (`push_down_predicate` on partition columns) vs **server-side catalog partition predicate** (`catalogPartitionPredicate`) for tables with huge partition counts ~.
- **Glue Studio** (visual), notebooks/interactive sessions, **DataBrew** (visual recipes), **Data Quality** (DQDL), **Schema Registry**, **sensitive data detection** transform, **workflows/triggers**.

## 3. Amazon EMR (skills 1.2.5, 3.3.6)
- Deployment: **EC2** (full control; primary + core + task nodes), **EKS** (Spark as pods on shared Kubernetes), **Serverless** (no cluster; per-job). Cluster node roles: primary (coordinates), core (HDFS/storage — keep On-Demand), task (stateless compute — Spot).
- Storage: S3 via EMRFS (decoupled storage), HDFS for scratch. Use Glue Data Catalog as Hive metastore ✓ (EMR integration).
- Scaling: managed scaling / auto scaling; instance fleets with Spot diversification; log URI to S3 so logs outlive the cluster.
- Lake Formation fine-grained access on EMR (incl. June 2026 direct S3 data access with EMR 7.13+ ✓ [WN]).
- **Release support** ✓ [EMR extended support](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/09/emr-extended-support-migration/): extended best-effort security fixes through 2027-06-30 for 5.36 and 6.6–6.15, and through 2027-08-31 for 7.0–7.10 — know "older releases still supported, migrate".
- Use EMR when: custom frameworks (HBase, Presto/Trino tuning), very large clusters with Spot economics, existing Hadoop/Spark code, specific JARs. Avoid when stem says "least operational overhead" and Glue/Serverless fits.

## 4. Lambda for transformation
Limits ✓ [Lambda quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/gettingstarted-limits.html): 15 min, 128–10,240 MB (1 vCPU at 1,769 MB), /tmp 512–10,240 MB, payload 6 MB sync / 1 MB async, concurrency 1,000 default, 1,000 environments/10 s scaling, zip 50 MB/250 MB unzipped, image 10 GB, layers 5. Good for: S3-triggered validation, Firehose transforms, small enrichments, API glue. Bad for: multi-GB joins, > 15 min.

## 5. Athena and Redshift as transformation engines
- **Athena CTAS**: `CREATE TABLE ... WITH (format='PARQUET', partitioned_by=ARRAY['dt'], external_location='s3://...') AS SELECT ...`; `INSERT INTO`; `UNLOAD` to write query results; Iceberg `MERGE`/`OPTIMIZE`/`VACUUM` ~. Limits ✓: query string 262,144 bytes; reads ≤ 1 M partitions per scan.
- **Redshift ELT**: `INSERT ... SELECT`, `MERGE`, stored procedures, materialized views, Spectrum for S3, COPY/UNLOAD; best when joins/aggregations dominate.

## 6. Containers: EKS and ECS (skill 1.2.1)
Use containers for custom runtimes, long jobs (> 15 min), shared platforms. **ECS on Fargate**: serverless containers, easy with Step Functions `.sync`; **EKS**: Kubernetes ecosystem, **EMR on EKS** for Spark on shared clusters; **ECR** stores images; **AWS Batch** schedules container jobs on EC2/Fargate/Spot. Optimise: right-size CPU/memory, Spot (Batch/EKS node groups), autoscaling (HPA/Karpenter/Cluster Autoscaler ~), image size for startup, place near data (same Region/AZ to avoid transfer cost).

## 7. Connecting and integrating sources (1.2.2, 1.2.3)
- **JDBC/ODBC**: Glue connections (JDBC URL, secret in Secrets Manager, VPC subnet + SG); Redshift/Athena JDBC/ODBC drivers for BI; partitioned reads for parallelism; push filters to source; use read replicas.
- **Integrate multiple sources**: Glue ETL joining JDBC + S3 + SaaS (AppFlow lands SaaS in S3); Athena **federated query** (Lambda connectors; "managed connectors" 12 sources Apr 2026 ~); Redshift Spectrum + federated query; zero-ETL for supported pairs ✓ (Aurora/RDS/DynamoDB/SaaS → Redshift/lakehouse); DMS for continuous DB → lake.
- Catalog as integration layer: Glue Data Catalog tables consumed by Athena/EMR/Redshift Spectrum/Glue.

## 8. Cost optimisation while processing (1.2.4)
| Lever | How |
|---|---|
| Right engine | Lambda < 15 min, Athena for SQL, Glue for Spark, EMR Spot for scale |
| Don't pay for idle | serverless (Glue, EMR Serverless, Athena, Redshift Serverless), auto scaling, Glue auto scaling, terminate transient EMR clusters |
| Cheaper capacity | Glue **Flex** ✓, EMR **Spot task nodes**, Savings Plans/RIs for steady, Redshift reservations (Serverless 3-yr up to 45 % ✓) |
| Read less data | Parquet/ORC, compression, partition pruning, pushdown, column selection |
| Fewer, larger files | compaction, Firehose buffering, `groupFiles` |
| Reduce egress | same-Region processing, VPC endpoints (gateway free ✓) vs NAT charges |

## 9. Format conversion (1.2.6)
CSV/JSON → **Parquet (Snappy)** partitioned by date. Where: Glue write with `format="parquet"`; Athena CTAS; Firehose record format conversion (needs Glue table); EMR Spark. Why: columnar pruning, compression, predicate pushdown, lower scan cost. Avro for row-oriented streaming + schema evolution; ORC for Hive/Presto; JSON/CSV for interchange only. Gzip is not splittable; multiple files or columnar fix single-file bottlenecks. See `cheatsheets/06-formats-compression.md`.

## 10. Troubleshooting transformations (1.2.7)
| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| Glue/Spark OOM on a few executors | data skew → salting, repartition, broadcast; or R.* / larger workers |
| Job reprocesses everything | bookmarks off/misconfigured; `transformation_ctx`, `job.commit()` |
| Slow listing / many tasks | small files → `groupFiles`/`groupSize`, compaction |
| One executor busy on single gzip file | non-splittable → split files/Parquet |
| S3 503 Slow Down | spread prefixes, fewer files, backoff ✓ |
| `AccessDenied` | role lacks S3/KMS/Glue permission; VPC endpoint policy |
| Cannot reach JDBC | subnet/SG/NAT/route; self-referencing SG ~ |
| Mixed types after upstream change | `ResolveChoice`, Schema Registry compatibility |
| Lambda timeout | > 15 min ✓ → Glue/Step Functions/Fargate; more memory = more CPU |
| Join slow | broadcast small side, AQE, correct join keys |
| Python import error in Glue | `--additional-python-modules` / `--extra-py-files` |
Monitoring: CloudWatch Logs (continuous logging), job metrics, Spark UI/history server, EventBridge Glue Job State Change → SNS.

## 11. Creating data APIs (1.2.8)
**API Gateway + Lambda + DynamoDB** for millisecond key lookups; API Gateway + Lambda + Athena (with cached/precomputed results) for analytics; throttling and usage plans protect backends; Cognito/IAM/Lambda authorizers for auth; Redshift Data API (HTTP, no drivers/connections ~) and Athena API for programmatic SQL; AppSync is out of scope ✓.

## 12. Volume, velocity, variety (1.2.9)
Volume → scale-out storage/compute, partitioning, columnar. Velocity → streaming (KDS/MSK/Flink), micro-batch. Variety → structured (tables), semi-structured (JSON/Avro/Parquet → DynamicFrame, SUPER), unstructured (documents/images/logs → S3 + schema-on-read, Macie/Textract/Comprehend for extraction). Pipeline design maps each V to a service choice.

## 13. LLMs in data processing (skill 1.2.10 — NEW in v1.1)
Exam stance: *integration patterns and trade-offs*, not API syntax (ML training/inference tasks are out of scope ✓ exam guide).
- Use cases in pipelines: classification/tagging of text, summarisation, entity/PII extraction, normalising messy fields, generating embeddings for vector stores, SQL generation assistance (Amazon Q).
- Where it plugs in: **Lambda or Step Functions task calling Amazon Bedrock** (InvokeModel/Converse) per record or batch; **Bedrock batch inference** (prompts in S3 → results in S3; cheaper and asynchronous for large nightly volumes ~); Glue/EMR jobs calling Bedrock in `mapPartitions` with throttling; **Bedrock Knowledge Bases** for managed RAG ingestion (S3 → chunk → embed → vector store); embeddings → Aurora pgvector / OpenSearch / MemoryDB / S3 Vectors ✓ (see D2 2.1.8/2.4.6).
- Operational concerns: throttling/quotas (retry with backoff, SQS buffering, max concurrency), token/cost control (batch, cache, smaller model), idempotency, data privacy (PII masking before prompts; VPC endpoints for Bedrock), output validation (schema checks, guardrails), non-determinism → store prompt/version with results.
- Pick: synchronous per-event enrichment → Lambda; bulk offline → batch inference; document Q&A → Knowledge Bases.

## 14. Worked scenarios
1. *2 TB/day CSV, custom PySpark, join to RDS, partitioned Parquet, no clusters* → **Glue Spark job** with JDBC connection, scheduled trigger (Lambda too small; EMR EC2 needs cluster; Athena can't do custom PySpark).
2. *Nightly job, can start hours late, reduce cost* → **Glue Flex** (G.1X/G.2X) ✓.
3. *Spark job on one 50 GB gzip file, one executor busy* → deliver multiple files or convert to Parquet (gzip not splittable).
4. *Classify 10 M tickets nightly, results to S3, not real time* → **Bedrock batch inference** (not per-record Lambda with unlimited concurrency).

## 15. Snippets (untested)
```sql
-- Athena CTAS: CSV -> partitioned Parquet
CREATE TABLE curated.orders
WITH (format='PARQUET', parquet_compression='SNAPPY',
      partitioned_by=ARRAY['dt'], external_location='s3://lake/curated/orders/') AS
SELECT order_id, customer_id, amount, CAST(order_ts AS date) AS dt FROM raw.orders_csv;
```
```python
# Glue: partitioned JDBC read for parallelism
df = glueContext.create_dynamic_frame.from_options(
  connection_type="postgresql",
  connection_options={"url": "jdbc:postgresql://host:5432/db", "dbtable": "orders",
     "secretId": "prod/orders-ro", "hashfield": "order_id", "hashpartitions": "16"})
```

## 16. Keyword → answer and traps
| Keyword | Answer | Trap |
|---|---|---|
| serverless Spark ETL | Glue | EMR on EC2 |
| non-urgent, lower price | Glue Flex | more workers |
| occasional Spark, own libs, no cluster | EMR Serverless | persistent EMR |
| Spark on existing Kubernetes | EMR on EKS | Glue |
| long container job, serverless | Fargate task via Step Functions `.sync` | Lambda |
| skewed key OOM | salting / repartition | add workers |
| many tiny files | groupFiles / compaction | bigger workers |
| mixed column types | ResolveChoice | drop column |
| bulk LLM scoring, offline | Bedrock batch inference | per-record sync calls |

# Task 1.3 — Orchestrate data pipelines (D1)
Tags: ✓ verified 2026-10-20 (link) · ~ established, not re-fetched. Skills 1.3.1–1.3.4 (+ 3.1.1/3.1.2/3.1.9 overlap).

## 1. Orchestrator selection (skill 1.3.1)
| | Step Functions | MWAA (Airflow) | Glue workflows | EventBridge (rules/Scheduler/Pipes) | Lambda |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Model | state machine (ASL JSON), visual | Python DAGs on managed Airflow | graph of crawlers/jobs/triggers | event routing, schedules | single function |
| Serverless | ✓ | ✗ (environment class, always-on) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Best for | AWS-native workflows, retries/catch, parallel/Map, human approval, SDK integrations (270+ services ✓ via Scheduler UTP; SFN has 200+ ~) | existing Airflow DAGs, rich scheduling/backfill, big operator ecosystem | Glue-only ETL chains | triggering/scheduling; light filtering/enrichment | tiny glue steps |
| Not for | very long polling (cost per transition) / Airflow portability | simple/short chains (idle cost) | non-Glue steps (Athena, Lambda…) | multi-step state, retries across steps | > 15 min ✓ |
| Pricing | per state transition (Standard) / requests+duration (Express) | environment-hours + workers | free (pay for jobs) | per event/invocation | per ms |
Decision: *AWS-native, serverless, least ops* → **Step Functions**. *Existing Airflow* → **MWAA**. *Only Glue* → **Glue workflows**. *Time/event trigger only* → **EventBridge**.

## 2. Step Functions ✓ [SFN quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/service-quotas.html)
- **Standard**: up to **1 year** execution, exactly-once workflow semantics ~, history ≤ **25,000 events**/execution (fails past it), history kept **90 days** after close, redrive window 14 days. **Express**: up to **5 minutes**, history unlimited but requires CloudWatch Logs, very high start rate (6,000 start burst), at-least-once (async) / at-most-once (sync) ~, no redrive.
- State input/output ≤ **256 KiB** → pass S3 pointers, not payloads.
- **Map**: inline (concurrency within history) vs **Distributed Map** (child executions; ≤ **10,000** parallel children; ≤ 1,000 open Map Runs) — the fix for large item sets/history limit.
- Resilience: `Retry` (ErrorEquals, IntervalSeconds, BackoffRate, MaxAttempts) then `Catch` → fallback/notify state; timeouts and heartbeats; `Choice` for branching; `Parallel`; `Wait`.
- Integrations: optimized (Lambda, Glue, EMR, ECS, Batch, Athena, SNS, SQS, DynamoDB, Bedrock ~); patterns `Request Response`, **`.sync`** (wait for job completion), **`.waitForTaskToken`** (callback for human approval/long external work — Standard only).
- Pricing note: Standard bills per state transition → polling loops with Wait are costly; prefer `.sync`/callbacks.

## 3. MWAA ✓ [MWAA environment class](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mwaa/latest/userguide/environment-class.html)
- Managed Apache Airflow; **environment class** sets Fargate worker/scheduler size and metadata DB: mw1.micro (≤25 DAGs, 3 tasks, no autoscaling), small (50/5), medium (250/10), large (1,000/20), xlarge (2,000/40), 2xlarge (4,000/80) — DAG capacity / default concurrent tasks. Schedulers 2–5 (1 for micro); triggerer runs with scheduler for **deferrable** operators/sensors.
- DAGs, plugins, requirements.txt live in an **S3 bucket** (dags/ folder); logs in CloudWatch Logs (scheduler, DAG processing, task, worker, webserver).
- Troubleshooting (3.1.2): DAG missing → DAG processing log import/syntax error or wrong path; package install failure → requirements.txt / VPC egress (NAT/endpoints for pip); task fails → task log + execution role permissions; slow → bigger class / more workers / `celery.worker_autoscale`.
- Use **sensors** (S3KeySensor, deferrable) to wait for files; **operators** for Glue, EMR, Athena, Redshift, Step Functions.
- Cost trap: always-on environment → not for infrequent, simple pipelines.

## 4. Glue workflows and triggers
Triggers: on-demand, scheduled (cron, UTC ~), conditional (job/crawler succeeded/failed), EventBridge event. Workflow = visual graph + shared run properties; supports **crawler → job → job**; no Lambda/Athena nodes. Good for self-contained Glue ETL; otherwise Step Functions.

## 5. EventBridge in orchestration
Rules (event patterns incl. S3, Glue Job State Change, Step Functions status, DMS, Redshift), **Scheduler** (time zones, one-time, flexible windows, retries ✓), **Pipes** (source → filter → enrich → target, e.g., DynamoDB Streams/SQS/Kinesis → Step Functions) ~, archive/replay ~, API destinations (call HTTP APIs with rate limit) ~. Event-driven pattern: **S3 → EventBridge → Step Functions** starts exactly when data arrives.

## 6. Pipelines for performance, availability, scalability, resiliency, fault tolerance (1.3.2)
| Quality | Techniques |
|---|---|
| Performance | parallel branches/Map, right-sized workers, partitioned data, avoid small files |
| Availability | managed multi-AZ services (S3, DynamoDB, Kinesis, SQS, Step Functions), multi-AZ MSK/Redshift RA3, cross-Region copies for DR |
| Scalability | on-demand Kinesis, Lambda concurrency, Glue auto scaling, SQS buffering, EMR managed scaling |
| Resiliency | retry w/ backoff + jitter, DLQs, circuit breakers, checkpoints, bookmarks, idempotent writes, quarantine bad records |
| Fault tolerance | decouple stages (SQS/S3 landing zones), redrive (SFN Standard redrive ✓ 14 d; SQS DLQ redrive), replayable raw data |

## 7. Serverless workflows (1.3.3)
Step Functions + Lambda + EventBridge + SQS/SNS + DynamoDB + S3 + Glue/Athena. Principles: event-driven, stateless functions, state in the workflow/DB, payload pointers, least-privilege per-state IAM, idempotency, observability (CloudWatch, SFN logging, X-Ray out of scope ✓). Human approval = callback task token (Standard). Long waits → Standard (up to 1 y) not Express.

## 8. Notifications (1.3.4)
**SNS** topic (email, SMS, HTTP, Lambda, SQS fan-out, mobile push; filter policies) for alerts and fan-out; **SQS** for durable buffering/decoupling and DLQs (1 MiB messages, retention 4 d default/14 d max, visibility 30 s default/12 h max ✓); EventBridge rules on failure events → SNS; CloudWatch alarms → SNS; Step Functions `Catch` → SNS publish task; Glue job notification/delay thresholds ✓.

## 9. Worked scenarios
1. *Glue job → Athena query → Lambda notify, retries and failure branching, serverless, least ops* → **Step Functions** (`.sync` Glue + Athena, Retry/Catch). Not MWAA (always-on), not Glue workflows (no Athena/Lambda).
2. *Dozens of existing Airflow DAGs, minimal rewrite* → **MWAA**.
3. *Workflow pauses days for a manager's approval* → **Standard workflow + task token** (Express ends at 5 min ✓).
4. *60,000-item Map hits 25,000-event history failure* → **Distributed Map** ✓.
5. *Wait for partner file without holding a worker slot* → MWAA deferrable S3 sensor; or S3 → EventBridge → Step Functions.

## 10. Snippets (untested)
```json
{ "StartAt": "RunGlue", "States": {
  "RunGlue": { "Type": "Task", "Resource": "arn:aws:states:::glue:startJobRun.sync",
    "Parameters": { "JobName": "curate-orders" },
    "Retry": [{ "ErrorEquals": ["States.TaskFailed"], "IntervalSeconds": 60, "BackoffRate": 2.0, "MaxAttempts": 3 }],
    "Catch": [{ "ErrorEquals": ["States.ALL"], "Next": "Notify" }], "Next": "Query" },
  "Query": { "Type": "Task", "Resource": "arn:aws:states:::athena:startQueryExecution.sync",
    "Parameters": { "QueryString": "SELECT count(*) FROM curated.orders", "WorkGroup": "primary" }, "End": true },
  "Notify": { "Type": "Task", "Resource": "arn:aws:states:::sns:publish",
    "Parameters": { "TopicArn": "arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:123456789012:alerts", "Message.$": "$" }, "End": true } } }
```

## 11. Keyword → answer and traps
| Keyword | Answer | Trap |
|---|---|---|
| serverless, retries, branching, AWS services | Step Functions | MWAA |
| existing Airflow | MWAA | rewrite to SFN |
| human approval / days | Standard + task token | Express |
| high-rate, < 5 min, idempotent | Express | Standard (cost) |
| huge Map / 25,000 events | Distributed Map | raise quota (hard limit) |
| Glue crawler → job chain only | Glue workflow | Step Functions (overkill, still valid) |
| cron with time zone | EventBridge Scheduler | rule cron (UTC) |
| fan-out with per-consumer DLQ | SNS → SQS | single queue |

# Task 1.4 — Apply programming concepts (D1)
Tags: ✓ verified 2026-10-20 (link) · ~ established. Skills 1.4.1–1.4.11. The exam tests *concepts and AWS tooling*, not language syntax ✓ (out of scope).

## 0. Skill map
1.4.1 optimise code §1 · 1.4.2 Lambda concurrency/performance §2 · 1.4.3 languages §3 · 1.4.4 software practices §4 · 1.4.5/1.4.8 IaC §5 · 1.4.6 SAM §6 · 1.4.7 mount volumes §7 · 1.4.9 CI/CD §8 · 1.4.10 distributed computing §9 · 1.4.11 data structures & algorithms §10

## 1. Optimise code to reduce runtime (1.4.1)
- **Lambda**: initialise SDK/DB clients **outside the handler** (reused across warm invocations); batch writes; reuse connections (RDS Proxy); more memory = more CPU (1 vCPU at 1,769 MB ✓); avoid heavy imports; use provisioned concurrency for cold starts; keep package small (zip 50 MB / 250 MB unzipped, image 10 GB ✓); ARM/Graviton for price-performance ~.
- **Spark/Glue**: filter early (pushdown predicates), select needed columns, broadcast small tables, avoid `collect()`/UDF row loops (prefer built-in functions/pandas UDF), tune shuffle partitions, repartition on join keys, handle skew (salting), cache only reused data, write fewer larger files (coalesce), use columnar formats.
- **SQL**: partition/sort-key filters, avoid `SELECT *`, pre-aggregate with MVs/CTAS, correct join order/keys, `LIMIT` for exploration, approximate functions (`approx_distinct`) ~.
- **I/O**: parallel multipart upload, byte-range reads, S3 prefixes for parallelism (3,500/5,500 req/s/prefix ✓), compression.

## 2. Lambda concurrency and performance (1.4.2) ✓ [Lambda quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/gettingstarted-limits.html)
| Concept | Facts |
|---|---|
| Account concurrency | 1,000 default per Region (soft); new accounts start lower |
| Scaling | each function adds up to 1,000 execution environments per 10 s |
| **Reserved concurrency** | guarantees *and caps* a function's share (also protects downstream DBs) |
| **Provisioned concurrency** | pre-initialised environments → no cold start (schedule with Application Auto Scaling for predictable peaks) |
| Sync invoke rate | ≤ 10 × concurrency requests/s |
| Event source mappings | SQS: set **maximum concurrency** on the mapping; Kinesis/DynamoDB: **ParallelizationFactor 1–10** ✓, batch size, batching window ≤ 5 min ✓ |
| Memory/CPU | 128–10,240 MB; CPU ∝ memory; Lambda power tuning to find the cost/latency sweet spot ~ |
| Timeout | 900 s; payload 6 MB sync / 1 MB async |
| Throttling (429) | async: automatic retries (2) then DLQ/on-failure destination ~; sync: caller retries |
| Idempotency | at-least-once triggers (S3, Kinesis ESM ✓, SQS) → idempotent handlers (conditional writes, Powertools idempotency ~) |
Protecting a database from Lambda scale-out: cap concurrency (reserved or ESM max), RDS Proxy, SQS buffer.

## 3. Languages and frameworks (1.4.3)
Python (boto3, pandas, PySpark, awswrangler ~), SQL (Athena/Presto-Trino, Redshift PostgreSQL-dialect), Scala/Java (Spark, Flink, Kafka), R (rare), Bash/PowerShell (CLI automation). AWS SDK concepts: paginators, waiters, retries/backoff, credentials chain, regions ✓ (skill 3.1.3). Choose by ecosystem: Spark → PySpark/Scala; Flink → Java/Python; glue scripts → Python.

## 4. Software engineering practices (1.4.4)
Version control (Git; CodeCommit removed from the exam scope list ✓ (AWS reports the service itself returned to GA in Nov 2025; scope and availability are separate) → GitHub/GitLab/CodeStar connections ~), branching, code review; **unit tests** (pytest on pure transformation functions, small fixtures; Glue Docker image/interactive sessions for local), integration tests in a dev account, data tests (Glue DQ/Deequ), **logging** (structured JSON to CloudWatch Logs), **monitoring** (CloudWatch metrics/alarms), config via parameters/Secrets Manager (no hard-coded secrets), idempotency and retries, small modules, documented schemas.

## 5. Infrastructure as code (1.4.5, 1.4.8)
| Tool | What | Pick when |
|---|---|---|
| **CloudFormation** | declarative JSON/YAML stacks, change sets, drift detection, StackSets for multi-account | baseline, all AWS resources |
| **CDK** | define stacks in Python/TS/Java/…; synthesises CloudFormation | developers want loops/abstractions/testing |
| **SAM** | CloudFormation transform for serverless (`AWS::Serverless::*`) + CLI for build/local test/deploy | Lambda/API/Step Functions/DynamoDB apps |
Why IaC: repeatable dev/test/prod (parameters), review in Git, rollback, no console drift. Typical data IaC: S3 buckets + Glue databases/jobs/crawlers + IAM roles + Step Functions + EventBridge rules + Lake Formation permissions.

## 6. AWS SAM (1.4.6)
`template.yaml` with `Transform: AWS::Serverless-2016-10-31`; resources `AWS::Serverless::Function`, `::StateMachine`, `::SimpleTable` (DynamoDB), `::Api`; commands `sam init`, `sam build`, `sam local invoke`, `sam deploy --guided`; event sources inline (S3, SQS, Kinesis, schedule). Use to package/deploy serverless data pipelines (Lambda + Step Functions + DynamoDB).
```yaml
Transform: AWS::Serverless-2016-10-31
Resources:
  Validate:
    Type: AWS::Serverless::Function
    Properties: { Handler: app.handler, Runtime: python3.13, MemorySize: 1024, Timeout: 120,
      Events: { Upload: { Type: S3, Properties: { Bucket: !Ref Landing, Events: s3:ObjectCreated:* } } } }
  Landing: { Type: AWS::S3::Bucket }
```
(untested; choose a currently supported runtime — runtime deprecation dates change, see `docs/exam-intel.md` §5.)

## 7. Mounting storage in Lambda (1.4.7)
- **Amazon EFS**: shared, persistent, POSIX file system mounted via access point; needs VPC config; use for large models/reference data updated outside deployments and shared by concurrent invocations.
- **/tmp ephemeral storage**: 512–10,240 MB per environment ✓, not shared, lost with environment.
- Layers (5 max, within 250 MB unzipped ✓) for libraries; container images up to 10 GB ✓; S3 for big objects (stream, don't load fully).

## 8. CI/CD for data pipelines (1.4.9)
CodePipeline (orchestrates stages) + CodeBuild (build/test/package, `buildspec.yml`) + CodeDeploy (Lambda/ECS/EC2 deployments, blue/green, canary/linear traffic shifting with alarms/rollback) + CloudFormation/CDK/SAM deploy; source: Git provider via connection (CodeCommit is no longer on the exam scope list ✓). Pipeline: lint → unit tests → package → deploy to dev → integration/data tests → approval → prod. Version artefacts (Glue scripts in S3 with version/prefix), use separate accounts per stage, parameterise env.

## 9. Distributed computing (1.4.10)
Split data into partitions processed in parallel (map), exchange data by key (shuffle), combine (reduce). Costs: shuffle (network + disk), skew (one hot key), small files, serialisation, memory spill. Techniques: partition by key, broadcast joins, salting, combiners/pre-aggregation, data locality (S3 is remote → minimise reads), idempotent tasks, fault tolerance by lineage/retry (Spark), checkpointing (Flink). Frameworks: Spark (Glue/EMR), Flink, Hive/Presto/Trino (Athena/EMR), MapReduce legacy.

## 10. Data structures and algorithms (1.4.11)
Know *where they appear*: **trees** (hierarchical data, B-tree indexes in RDS, partition/zone-map pruning), **graphs** (relationship traversal → Neptune; lineage graphs; DAG workflows in Airflow/Step Functions), **hash tables/partitioning** (shard routing by partition key hash, DynamoDB), **bloom filters** (dedupe, Parquet/ORC row-group skipping ~), **sorting/merge** (sort keys, compaction), **queues/streams** (SQS/Kinesis), **approximate nearest neighbour** (HNSW graph, IVF clusters — vector search, D2 2.1.8). Complexity intuition: O(n) full scan vs O(log n) index vs O(1) key lookup → pick DynamoDB/index for point lookups, columnar scans for aggregates.

## 11. Worked scenarios
1. *Lambda inserts rows; slow and costly* → move client init outside handler, batch inserts (and RDS Proxy).
2. *Same Glue job, IAM role, bucket across dev/test/prod* → parameterised **CloudFormation/CDK** template, pipeline per environment.
3. *Lambda needs to unzip an 8 GB archive* → ephemeral storage up to 10,240 MB ✓.
4. *SQS-triggered Lambda exhausts RDS connections* → ESM **maximum concurrency** + RDS Proxy.
5. *Java Lambda with 08:00 cold-start spike* → **provisioned concurrency** with scheduled scaling.

## 12. Keyword → answer and traps
| Keyword | Answer | Trap |
|---|---|---|
| reuse connections / faster Lambda | init outside handler, batching | more timeout |
| cap concurrency to protect DB | reserved concurrency / ESM max concurrency | memory increase |
| no cold start, predictable peak | provisioned concurrency | reserved |
| shared large mutable files | EFS | layer / zip |
| repeatable environments | CloudFormation / CDK | console clicks |
| serverless app package/test locally | SAM | plain CFN scripts |
| testing Spark logic fast | pure functions + pytest + small data | run full job |
| point lookup vs scan | key-value/index | full scan |

# Task 2.1 — Choose a data store (Domain 2 = 26 %)
Tags: ✓ verified 2026-10-20 (link) · ~ established, not re-fetched. Skills 2.1.1–2.1.8.

## 0. Skill map
2.1.1 cost/perf selection §1–§5 · 2.1.2 access-pattern configuration §3–§4 · 2.1.3 use cases (HNSW/Aurora, MemoryDB) §5, §9 · 2.1.4 migration tools §7 · 2.1.5 remote access §3 · 2.1.6 locks §8 · 2.1.7 open table formats §6 · 2.1.8 vector index types §9

## 1. Selection by access pattern (master table)
| Access pattern / need | Choose | Why | Not |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ad hoc SQL on rarely queried lake data | **S3 + Athena** | pay per TB scanned, no infra | provisioned Redshift |
| Repeated BI, complex joins, high concurrency, columnar warehouse | **Redshift** (+ Spectrum for cold S3) | MPP, MVs, concurrency scaling | RDS/Aurora |
| Key-value/document, known access paths, ms latency, any scale | **DynamoDB** | serverless, partition key design | relational joins |
| Relational OLTP, transactions, joins | **RDS / Aurora** | SQL, ACID, replicas | analytics at scale |
| Wide-column, Cassandra/CQL | **Keyspaces** | serverless Cassandra-compatible | DynamoDB (different API) |
| MongoDB-compatible documents | **DocumentDB** | | DynamoDB |
| Graph traversal (fraud rings, recommendations) | **Neptune** | multi-hop relationship queries | Redshift joins |
| Durable microsecond Redis-compatible primary DB | **MemoryDB** | multi-AZ durable, sorted sets, vector search ~ | S3 |
| Log/search/dashboards, near-real-time text | **OpenSearch Service** | inverted index, k-NN | Athena (latency) |
| Streams as storage (replayable log) | **KDS / MSK** | retention (KDS 24 h–365 d ✓) | S3 |
| Data lake files / archive | **S3** classes ✓ | 11 9's durability | EBS/EFS |
| Managed Iceberg tables | **S3 Tables** ✓ | auto maintenance | self-managed small files |
| Time series | (Timestream no longer in either scope list ✓) | treat as DynamoDB/S3+Athena/OpenSearch patterns | — |
Cost/performance levers: serverless vs provisioned, reservations, storage tier, compression, partitioning, caching (DAX, ElastiCache not in scope list).

## 2. S3 storage classes ✓ [S3 storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html)
| Class | Designed for | AZs | Availability | Min duration | Min size | Retrieval |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Standard | frequent, ms | ≥3 | 99.99 % | none | none | none |
| Intelligent-Tiering | unknown/changing patterns | ≥3 | 99.9 % | none | monitoring fee; **objects < 128 KB not monitored** | **no retrieval fee**; tiers: Frequent → Infrequent (30 d) → Archive Instant Access (90 d) → optional Archive Access (≥ 90 d) / Deep Archive Access (≥ 180 d, need RestoreObject) |
| Standard-IA | infrequent monthly, ms | ≥3 | 99.9 % | **30 d** | **128 KB** | per-GB fee |
| One Zone-IA | re-creatable infrequent, ms | **1** | 99.5 % | 30 d | 128 KB | per-GB fee; not AZ-resilient (good CRR replica target) |
| **Express One Zone** | single-digit-ms hot data, directory buckets | **1** | 99.95 % | none | none | up to 10× faster, 50 % lower request cost than Standard |
| Glacier Instant Retrieval | quarterly, ms | ≥3 | 99.9 % | **90 d** | 128 KB | per-GB fee |
| Glacier Flexible Retrieval | yearly, min–hours | ≥3 | 99.99 % after restore | **90 d** | 40 KB metadata/object (8 KB Standard + 32 KB Glacier) | restore needed (Expedited / Standard / Bulk ~) |
| Glacier Deep Archive | < yearly, hours | ≥3 | 99.99 % after restore | **180 d** | 40 KB metadata | restore needed (Standard / Bulk ~) |
All Standard-family classes: 11 nines durability. Early deletion/transition → pro-rated charge ✓. S3 request rates ✓: 3,500 writes / 5,500 reads per second per prefix. Reduced Redundancy: don't use ✓.
Shortcuts: "unknown pattern, no retrieval fees" → **Intelligent-Tiering**; "quarterly, ms" → **Glacier IR**; "re-creatable, cheaper than IA" → **One Zone-IA**; "archive, hours OK, cheapest" → **Deep Archive**; "ML training hot data single-AZ ms" → **Express One Zone**.

## 3. Amazon Redshift (2.1.1, 2.1.2, 2.1.5)
- **Provisioned (RA3, managed storage)** for steady load/reservations; **Serverless** (RPUs) for spiky/dev, 3-year reservations up to 45 % ✓ (Feb 2026). **Concurrency scaling** for read bursts. Security: TLS ≥1.2 enforced from 2026-10-31 ✓.
- **Spectrum**: query S3 via external schemas/tables in the Glue Data Catalog; join with local tables; cold-data tiering (UNLOAD old data → Parquet → Spectrum).
- **Federated query**: live read of RDS/Aurora PostgreSQL & MySQL. **Materialized views**: precompute; auto refresh; can sit on Spectrum/external tables ~; streaming ingestion MVs from KDS/MSK ✓.
- **Data sharing** ✓ [Redshift data sharing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/dg/datashare-overview.html): live, transactionally consistent access **across clusters, serverless workgroups, AZs, accounts and Regions with no copy**; share databases/schemas/tables/views (regular, late-binding, materialized)/SQL UDFs/stored procedures; **read AND now write** (INSERT/UPDATE) shares (older material says read-only); use cases: central ETL → many BI clusters (workload isolation + chargeback), dev/test/prod sharing, Data Exchange licensing. Steps: producer `CREATE DATASHARE`, add objects, `GRANT USAGE ON DATASHARE … TO ACCOUNT/NAMESPACE`, (cross-account: authorize), consumer `CREATE DATABASE … FROM DATASHARE`.
- **Zero-ETL** from Aurora/RDS/DynamoDB/SaaS into Redshift ✓ (continuous, no pipeline).
- Python UDFs: end of support after 2026-06-30 ✓ → Lambda UDFs.
Deep Redshift design (dist/sort keys, COPY/UNLOAD, WLM, troubleshooting): `cheatsheets/07-redshift.md`, §D2 2.4.

## 4. Amazon DynamoDB (2.1.2) ✓ [DDB quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/ServiceQuotas.html)
- Capacity: **on-demand** (unpredictable, least ops) vs **provisioned + auto scaling** (+ reserved capacity) for steady predictable load = cheapest. Defaults ✓: 40,000 RCU/WCU per table; 80,000 per account (provisioned); 2,500 tables/Region; 5 LSI; 20 GSI; ≤ 2 Streams readers per shard; PITR to any second within up to 35 days ~; global tables (MREC/MRSC) for multi-Region; TTL free expiry; DAX read cache ~.
- RCU/WCU maths ~: 1 RCU = one strongly consistent 4 KB read/s (eventual = ½, transactional = 2×); 1 WCU = one 1 KB write/s (transactional 2×). Item max 400 KB ~.
- Design rule: start from query list. See 2.4 for key design, GSIs, hot partitions.
- Vector indexes ✓ (DynamoDB quotas page): ≤ 5 per table, ≤ 4,096 dimensions, TopK ≤ 100, ≤ 18 inline filters.

## 5. RDS / Aurora (2.1.1, 2.1.3)
RDS engines (MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Oracle, SQL Server, Db2 ~) — Multi-AZ (failover standby; sync), read replicas (async, scale reads). **Aurora**: shared distributed storage, up to 15 replicas ~, fast failover, Global Database, serverless v2, **Aurora PostgreSQL + pgvector** ✓. RDS Proxy pools connections (Lambda/serverless clients). Zero-ETL Aurora/RDS → Redshift. Choose Aurora when you need higher scale/HA/replicas or pgvector HNSW; RDS when engine-specific compatibility (Oracle/SQL Server) or simple lift-and-shift.

## 6. Open table formats and S3 Tables (2.1.7 — NEW v1.1)
| | Iceberg | Delta Lake | Hudi |
|---|---|---|---|
| Strengths | hidden partitioning, partition & schema evolution, snapshots (time travel/rollback), ACID, engine-neutral | ACID + time travel, Spark-centric | record-level upserts, incremental pulls, COW/MOR |
| Support | Athena, Redshift, EMR, Glue, Snowflake… | Glue/EMR/Athena | Glue/EMR/Athena |
Glue 5.1 bundles Iceberg 1.10.0, Hudi 1.0.2, Delta 3.3.2 ✓.
**S3 Tables** ✓ [S3 Tables](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/s3-tables.html): new **table bucket** type; tables stored as **Apache Iceberg** (incl. V3: deletion vectors, row lineage, column defaults, variant/geometry/geography/nanosecond timestamps); higher TPS and query throughput than self-managed tables in general-purpose buckets; **automatic maintenance** (compaction, snapshot management, unreferenced-file removal; configurable); IAM/SCP in the **`s3tables`** namespace, table-level policies; **Block Public Access always on**; integrates with Glue Data Catalog → Athena, Redshift, EMR, Glue, Quick, Lake Formation, SageMaker Unified Studio; Intelligent-Tiering for tables; replication of tables.
Iceberg operations in Athena ~: `CREATE TABLE … TBLPROPERTIES('table_type'='ICEBERG')`, `MERGE`, `DELETE`, `OPTIMIZE … REWRITE DATA USING BIN_PACK`, `VACUUM`, time travel `FOR TIMESTAMP AS OF`. Governed tables (old LF feature) → replaced by Iceberg.
Pick: need ACID/upserts/time travel on S3 → Iceberg; least ops managed Iceberg → **S3 Tables**; heavy upsert/CDC on Spark → Hudi (or Iceberg MERGE); Databricks interoperability → Delta.

## 7. Migration and transfer tools (2.1.4)
| Need | Tool |
|---|---|
| Database migration (homogeneous/heterogeneous), CDC | **DMS** (+ DMS Schema Conversion) |
| Online file/object sync on a schedule (NFS/SMB/HDFS/S3/EFS/FSx), verification, bandwidth control | **DataSync** |
| Partners push files over SFTP/FTPS/FTP/AS2 into S3/EFS | **Transfer Family** (managed endpoint; custom identity provider; also integrates as a migration entry point into pipelines) |
| Petabytes offline / poor network | **Snow Family** |
| SaaS data | **AppFlow** |
| Servers lift-and-shift | Application Migration Service |
| Third-party data subscriptions | Data Exchange |

## 8. Locks (2.1.6)
- **Redshift**: DDL/TRUNCATE take exclusive locks; long open transactions block others; find with `STV_LOCKS`, `SVV_TRANSACTIONS`, `STV_RECENTS`; clear with `PG_TERMINATE_BACKEND(pid)`; keep transactions short; concurrent writes serialize per table (snapshot isolation / serializable ~).
- **RDS/Aurora**: row/table locks, deadlocks (InnoDB, PostgreSQL); resolve by consistent access order, short transactions, retries; inspect `SHOW ENGINE INNODB STATUS` / `pg_locks`/`pg_stat_activity` ~.
- **DynamoDB**: no locks; use **conditional writes** (optimistic locking with a version attribute) and transactions.

## 9. Vector index types (2.1.8 — NEW) and where vectors live (2.1.3)
- **Embedding**: model-generated numeric vector; similarity metrics: cosine, L2 (Euclidean), inner product. Exact kNN is O(n); **approximate** nearest neighbour (ANN) trades recall for speed.
- **HNSW** (Hierarchical Navigable Small World): multi-layer proximity graph; **high recall, fast queries, more memory, slower build**; tunables m, ef_construction (recommended 256 with pgvector ≥ 0.6.0 ✓), ef_search. **IVF/IVFFlat**: k-means style clusters (lists); query probes nearest lists (probes); **faster build, less memory, lower recall at same latency, needs data first** ~.
- Aurora PostgreSQL ✓ [Aurora pgvector / Bedrock KB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/AuroraPostgreSQL.VectorDB.html): `CREATE EXTENSION vector;` (**pgvector ≥ 0.5.0 for HNSW**); `CREATE INDEX … USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops) WITH (ef_construction=256);` supported in Aurora PostgreSQL 16.1+, 15.4+, 14.9+, 13.12+, 12.16+; table typically `(id uuid pk, embedding vector(n), chunks text, metadata json, custom_metadata jsonb)` with GIN index on `to_tsvector('simple', chunks)`; embedding dimensions: Titan v2 256/512/1024, Titan multimodal 1536, Cohere Embed 1024 ✓; requires RDS Data API + Secrets Manager secret when used as a Bedrock Knowledge Base.
- Other vector stores: OpenSearch (k-NN), **MemoryDB** (vector search, durable, µs) ~, **DynamoDB vector indexes** ✓, **S3 Vectors** (GA Dec 2025; low-cost large scale ~), Bedrock Knowledge Bases (managed). **MemoryDB** also the answer for "fast key/value with durability".
- Pick: SQL app + relational joins → Aurora pgvector (HNSW for recall); managed RAG → Knowledge Bases; ultra-low latency/leaderboards → MemoryDB; cheap huge cold vector sets → S3 Vectors.

## 10. Worked scenarios
1. *50 TB history, a few ad hoc queries/month, least cost, no infra* → **S3 Parquet + Athena**.
2. *Quarterly access, ms retrieval, 5-year retention* → lifecycle Standard → **Glacier Instant Retrieval** (90-day minimum satisfied) ✓.
3. *Unknown/changing access, no retrieval fees, >128 KB objects* → **Intelligent-Tiering**.
4. *Producer team shares Redshift tables live with another account* → **data sharing** (not UNLOAD/snapshot).
5. *Aurora PostgreSQL semantic search, 5 M embeddings, best recall* → **pgvector HNSW**.
6. *Cassandra app, serverless, minimal change* → **Keyspaces**; *fraud rings* → **Neptune**; *Redis-compatible durable* → **MemoryDB**.

## 11. Keyword → answer and traps
| Keyword | Answer | Trap |
|---|---|---|
| unknown access, no retrieval fee | Intelligent-Tiering | Standard-IA (retrieval fee) |
| re-creatable, cheaper IA | One Zone-IA | Standard-IA |
| quarterly + ms | Glacier IR | Flexible (restore) |
| live cross-account warehouse sharing | Redshift data sharing | UNLOAD |
| query S3 from Redshift | Spectrum | federated query (RDS only) |
| live RDS data in Athena/Redshift | federated query | crawler |
| managed Iceberg + auto compaction | S3 Tables | self-managed Iceberg |
| upsert + time travel on S3 | Iceberg/Hudi | plain Parquet |
| optimistic locking DynamoDB | conditional write | table lock |
| SFTP partners | Transfer Family | DataSync |
| high-recall ANN, memory OK | HNSW | IVF / B-tree / GIN |

<!-- source: guide/D2-data-store-management/2.2-catalog.md -->

# Task 2.2 — Understand data cataloging systems (D2)
Tags: ✓ verified 2026-10-20 · ~ established, not re-fetched. Skills 2.2.1–2.2.6.

## 1. Two kinds of catalog (know the difference)
| | Technical catalog | Business catalog |
|---|---|---|
| Service | **AWS Glue Data Catalog** (Hive-metastore-compatible), Apache Hive metastore | **Amazon SageMaker Catalog** (in SageMaker Unified Studio; built on DataZone) |
| Holds | databases, tables, columns/types, partitions, connections, schema versions | business glossary, metadata forms, data products/assets, ownership, subscriptions/approvals, lineage |
| Consumers | Athena, Redshift Spectrum, EMR, Glue, Lake Formation, Quick | analysts/data consumers across projects |
| Skills | 2.2.1–2.2.5 | 2.2.6 (NEW v1.1), 2.4.4, 4.5.6 |

## 2. Glue Data Catalog (2.2.1, 2.2.2)
- One catalog per account/Region (cross-account via Lake Formation/RAM resource links); tables point to data in S3 (also JDBC, Kinesis, Kafka schemas); **Hive-compatible** so EMR/Hive/Spark/Presto can use it as external metastore ✓ (Glue job option "Use Glue Data Catalog as the Hive metastore", EMR setting).
- **Consume data from source via catalog (2.2.1)**: Athena `SELECT` on a catalog table; Glue `create_dynamic_frame.from_catalog`; Redshift Spectrum external schema `FROM DATA CATALOG`; EMR Spark `spark.sql` with Glue metastore; Quick datasets. Catalog = schema + location + format (SerDe) + partitions.
- Tables created by: crawlers, Athena/Hive DDL, Glue ETL (`enableUpdateCatalog`; not with LF cell-level filters ✓), console/API/CloudFormation, S3 Tables integration ✓, zero-ETL.
- **Encryption & access**: catalog encryption (KMS), resource policy for cross-account, Lake Formation permissions for fine-grained access.

## 3. Crawlers (2.2.3) — schema discovery
- Crawl S3/JDBC/DynamoDB/etc.; **classifiers** (built-in CSV/JSON/Parquet/Avro/ORC…, custom grok/JSON/XML/CSV); infer schema; create/update **tables and partitions**; one table per consistent prefix; **schema change policy**: update table definition vs **log only**; deletion behaviour (delete from catalog / mark deprecated / ignore).
- Run: on demand, scheduled, or event-driven (S3 events ~); **incremental crawl** (only new folders) ~; sample size options; exclusion patterns; JDBC via connection.
- Typical issues: mixed schemas under one prefix → separate prefixes/exclusions; crawler slow on huge prefixes → incremental/targeted crawl or **partition projection**; type drift → custom classifier or manual DDL.
- Crawler vs manual DDL: DDL is deterministic and free; crawler convenient for unknown/evolving schemas.

## 4. Partitions (2.2.4)
Options to keep the catalog in sync with S3 layouts like `dt=YYYY-MM-DD/`:
| Method | When | Cost/limits |
|---|---|---|
| Crawler | unknown layouts | slow/costly at scale |
| `MSCK REPAIR TABLE` | many Hive-style prefixes added | scans all prefixes |
| `ALTER TABLE ADD PARTITION` (Lambda on S3 event / ETL job) | known partition added | precise, cheap |
| **Partition projection** (Athena table properties) | predictable patterns (date/int/enum) | no catalog partitions, fastest planning; Athena-specific |
| **Glue partition indexes** ~ | millions of catalog partitions | speeds partition lookups |
| ETL `enableUpdateCatalog` + `partitionKeys` | writer adds partitions | |
Limits ✓: Athena can read tables with 10 M partitions but **not more than 1 M in one scan**. Over-partitioning → small files, slow planning; design partitions on filter columns with moderate cardinality.

## 5. Connections (2.2.5)
Glue **connections** store JDBC/ODBC/Kafka/Snowflake/MongoDB/etc. connection properties (secret in Secrets Manager ✓ reference), network config (VPC, subnet, security groups). Crawlers and jobs use them. On-prem DB over VPN/Direct Connect → connection in a VPC subnet with route to it; SG must allow traffic (self-referencing SG for Glue ENIs ~); S3 gateway endpoint/NAT for S3 access.

## 6. Business data catalogs (2.2.6 — NEW) ✓ secondary-verified [UNVERIFIED details in open-questions]
**Amazon SageMaker Catalog** (successor of the DataZone catalog; V2 domains open in SageMaker Unified Studio): 
- Concepts: **domain** (top boundary) → **domain units** (org groups) → **projects** (team workspace with members/roles, compute, assets); **assets/data products** are *published* with business metadata (glossary terms, metadata forms); consumers **search and subscribe**; the owner **approves**; for *managed* assets (Glue/Lake Formation or Redshift) the catalog **provisions grants** automatically; supports custom asset types (e.g., dashboards, PDFs) in IAM-based domains (2026).
- Identity: IAM Identity Center–based or IAM-based domains.
- **Lineage** (OpenLineage-compatible ~) shows upstream/downstream datasets and jobs (skill 2.4.4).
- Contrast: Glue Data Catalog answers "what is the schema and where is it"; SageMaker Catalog answers "who owns it, what does it mean, how do I get access".
Distractor logic: CloudTrail/Config are not catalogs; Glue crawlers populate technical metadata only; Macie classifies S3 data but isn't a business catalog.

## 7. Worked scenarios
1. *New daily partitions invisible in Athena until the crawler runs; pattern predictable* → **partition projection**.
2. *Crawler changed production columns and broke queries* → crawler policy **Log**, review and apply DDL manually.
3. *EMR and Athena must share table definitions* → EMR uses **Glue Data Catalog** as Hive metastore.
4. *Business glossary + subscription approval + lineage across teams* → **SageMaker Catalog**.
5. *Millions of partitions, slow Athena planning* → **partition indexes** or projection.

## 8. Snippets (untested)
```sql
-- Athena partition projection
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE events (id string, payload string)
PARTITIONED BY (dt string)
STORED AS PARQUET LOCATION 's3://lake/events/'
TBLPROPERTIES ('projection.enabled'='true','projection.dt.type'='date',
  'projection.dt.range'='2025-01-01,NOW','projection.dt.format'='yyyy-MM-dd',
  'storage.location.template'='s3://lake/events/dt=${dt}/');
```
```bash
aws glue create-crawler --name crawl-orders --role GlueCrawlerRole --database-name raw \
  --targets '{"S3Targets":[{"Path":"s3://lake/raw/orders/"}]}' \
  --schema-change-policy '{"UpdateBehavior":"LOG","DeleteBehavior":"LOG"}' \
  --recrawl-policy '{"RecrawlBehavior":"CRAWL_NEW_FOLDERS_ONLY"}'
```

## 9. Keyword → answer and traps
| Keyword | Answer | Trap |
|---|---|---|
| shared metastore for EMR/Athena | Glue Data Catalog | separate Hive metastore |
| predictable date partitions, avoid crawler | partition projection | MSCK every hour |
| review schema changes | crawler Log policy | update table automatically |
| business glossary, subscriptions, lineage | SageMaker Catalog | Glue Data Catalog |
| cross-account tables | Lake Formation share + resource link | copy data |
| JDBC source cataloging | Glue connection + crawler | S3 event |

<!-- source: guide/D2-data-store-management/2.3-lifecycle.md -->

# Task 2.3 — Manage the lifecycle of data (D2)
Tags: ✓ verified 2026-10-20 (link) · ~ established, not re-fetched. Skills 2.3.1–2.3.6.

## 1. Redshift ↔ S3: load and unload (2.3.1)
**COPY** (S3 → Redshift): parallel across slices; use **many compressed files, ideally a multiple of the slice count**; point at a prefix or **manifest**; IAM role attached to cluster; formats CSV/JSON/Parquet/ORC/Avro; options `COMPUPDATE`, `STATUPDATE`, `MAXERROR`; **auto-copy** (continuous ingestion from S3 prefix ~). A single huge file loads on one slice → slow ✓. INSERT row-by-row is the anti-pattern.
**UNLOAD** (Redshift → S3): parallel by default, `FORMAT PARQUET`, `PARTITION BY (col)`, encryption/KMS, `MAXFILESIZE`, `MANIFEST`. Use for archiving cold data then Spectrum, or feeding the lake.
**Upsert**: stage table → `MERGE` (or delete+insert in a transaction). **Glue/Redshift connector** uses an S3 temp path. **Spectrum** avoids loading cold data at all.
```sql
COPY sales FROM 's3://lake/curated/sales/dt=2026-10-19/' IAM_ROLE 'arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/RedshiftCopy' FORMAT AS PARQUET;
UNLOAD ('SELECT * FROM sales WHERE sale_date < ''2025-01-01''') TO 's3://lake/archive/sales/'
  IAM_ROLE 'arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/RedshiftCopy' FORMAT PARQUET PARTITION BY (sale_date);
```

## 2. S3 Lifecycle: transitions and expiration (2.3.2, 2.3.3) ✓ [Lifecycle transitions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/lifecycle-transition-general-considerations.html)
- **Waterfall** transitions: Standard → IA / Intelligent-Tiering / One Zone-IA / Glacier IR / Glacier FR / Deep Archive; Standard-IA → INT / ZIA / GIR / GFR / GDA; GIR → GFR / GDA; One Zone-IA → GFR / GDA; **GFR → only Deep Archive**; **Deep Archive is one-way** (restore + copy to change class). Intelligent-Tiering tiers move automatically (30 d / 90 d / 180 d ✓).
- **Objects < 128 KB don't transition by default** (since Sep 2024) — use `ObjectSizeGreaterThan/LessThan` filters to override; you pay a request charge per transition, so tiny objects can cost more than they save.
- **Minimum storage durations** (early transition/deletion → pro-rated charge ✓): IA/One Zone-IA 30 d, Glacier IR 90 d, GFR 90 d, GDA 180 d. A rule can't move an object out of a class before its minimum duration in one step (e.g., GIR 90 d then GDA → at least 94 d if first transition at day 4).
- Glacier FR/GDA add **40 KB metadata per object** (8 KB billed at Standard + 32 KB at Glacier rate) → aggregate small objects before archiving ✓.
- Transitions are **asynchronous**; billing at destination rate starts when the rule is met even if the physical move is later ✓. Rule changes can take up to ~15 min to propagate ✓. Tag filters are re-evaluated at execution ✓.
- **Expiration**: `Expiration` (current versions → delete marker in versioned buckets), `NoncurrentVersionExpiration`/`NoncurrentVersionTransition`, `ExpiredObjectDeleteMarker` cleanup, `AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload`, `NewerNoncurrentVersions` retention count.
- Restore: archived objects need `RestoreObject` (temporary copy billed at Standard; archive still billed) ✓; tiers Expedited/Standard/Bulk ~.
```json
{"Rules":[{"ID":"logs","Status":"Enabled","Filter":{"Prefix":"logs/"},
 "Transitions":[{"Days":30,"StorageClass":"GLACIER_IR"}],"Expiration":{"Days":1825},
 "NoncurrentVersionExpiration":{"NoncurrentDays":30},
 "AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload":{"DaysAfterInitiation":7}}]}
```

## 3. Versioning and TTL (2.3.4)
- **S3 versioning**: keeps all versions; delete creates a **delete marker**; enable with MFA delete ~; required for CRR/SRR; storage cost grows → lifecycle noncurrent expiration; `Object Lock` (WORM, governance/compliance modes, legal hold) for retention mandates ~; versioning can be suspended, not removed.
- **DynamoDB TTL**: set an epoch-seconds attribute; background deletion at no WCU cost; deletion typically within a few days of expiry ✓ (docs); expired items may still appear until deleted (filter in queries); deletions appear in Streams (can archive to S3 via Streams/Firehose); not for exact-time deletion.
- Also: Kinesis retention (24 h–365 d ✓), SQS retention (default 4 d, 60 s–14 d ✓), CloudWatch Logs retention, Redshift snapshot retention, Iceberg `expire_snapshots`.

## 4. Deleting data for business/legal requirements (2.3.5)
- Retention/erasure patterns: S3 lifecycle expiration; Object Lock legal hold (the opposite: prevents deletion); DynamoDB TTL; **right-to-erasure** in lakes: Iceberg/Hudi/Delta row-level `DELETE` then **expire snapshots/remove orphan files** (otherwise old snapshots still hold the data) ✓ (D2 topic-set Q32); for plain Parquet rewrite affected partitions; also remove from backups/replicas/caches/derived tables (and embeddings in vector stores).
- Find the data: Macie (S3 PII discovery), Glue sensitive data detection, catalog tags/LF-tags, lineage.
- Audit: CloudTrail data events, S3 Inventory ~, Config.

## 5. Resiliency and availability (2.3.6)
| Store | Features |
|---|---|
| S3 | 11 9's durability, ≥3 AZ (except One Zone classes ✓); versioning; **CRR/SRR** (async, needs versioning; replicate to One Zone-IA to save; replication time control ~); Object Lock; Multi-Region Access Points ~ |
| DynamoDB | multi-AZ by default; **PITR (up to 35 d ~)**, on-demand backups, **global tables** (MREC/MRSC ✓ quotas), AWS Backup |
| Redshift | automated + manual snapshots, **cross-Region snapshot copy** (encrypted needs KMS **snapshot copy grant** in destination), RA3 managed storage, Multi-AZ RA3 ~, restore to new cluster |
| RDS/Aurora | Multi-AZ, read replicas, automated backups + PITR, snapshots (copy/share cross-Region/account; encrypted need shared CMK), **Aurora Global Database**, RDS Proxy |
| Kinesis/MSK | replicated across 3 AZs ~; retention is your replay buffer; MSK Replicator for cross-cluster/Region ✓ |
| EBS/EFS | snapshots / multi-AZ + AWS Backup |
| Org-wide | **AWS Backup**: policies, cross-Region and cross-account copy, **Vault Lock**, supports S3, DynamoDB, RDS/Aurora, Redshift, EFS… ~ |
DR strategies by RPO/RTO: backup & restore → pilot light → warm standby → multi-site active-active. Residency constraint → restrict copies to approved Regions (SCP, replication rules, backup plans) (4.5.3).

## 6. Worked scenarios
1. *Audit logs: hot 30 days, quarterly access (ms), keep 5 y, then delete* → lifecycle Standard → **GLACIER_IR** at 30 d, expire at 1,825 d ✓.
2. *Versioned bucket growing; old versions needed only 30 d; leftover multipart uploads* → **NoncurrentVersionExpiration 30 d + AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload**.
3. *Session items expire after 24 h, free* → **DynamoDB TTL**.
4. *Encrypted Redshift DR to another Region* → cross-Region snapshot copy + **snapshot copy grant** with destination KMS key.
5. *5-year-old Redshift data, still queryable, cheaper* → **UNLOAD Parquet → S3 + Spectrum**.
6. *Erase a customer from Iceberg lake* → **DELETE + expire snapshots + remove orphans**.

## 7. Keyword → answer and traps
| Keyword | Answer | Trap |
|---|---|---|
| COPY slow, one file | split into multiple files = multiple of slices | bigger nodes |
| archive old Redshift data but query it | UNLOAD + Spectrum | DELETE + VACUUM |
| expire noncurrent versions | lifecycle NoncurrentVersionExpiration | disable versioning (impossible) |
| auto-expire items for free | DynamoDB TTL | scheduled Lambda scan |
| DR copy of S3 in another Region | CRR (+ versioning) | Transfer Acceleration |
| cheapest archive, hours OK | Deep Archive (180 d) | Glacier IR |
| small files lifecycle | filter / aggregate first | transition everything |
| erasure in Iceberg | delete + expire snapshots | drop metadata file |
