# Task 2.4 — Design data models and schema evolution (D2)
Tags: ✓ verified 2026-10-20 (link) · ~ established, not re-fetched. Skills 2.4.1–2.4.6.

## 1. Schema design (2.4.1)
### Redshift
| Decision | Guidance |
|---|---|
| **Distribution** | AUTO (default) · KEY on the common join column of two big tables (co-location; avoid skewed keys) · ALL for small, slowly-changing dimensions · EVEN when no join key |
| **Sort key** | compound (leading-column filters; typical `date`) vs interleaved (equal weight across columns; slower loads, rare) vs AUTO; zone maps skip blocks |
| Compression | encodings AUTO; Parquet/ORC for external |
| Keys | PK/FK **informational, not enforced** ~ |
| Semi-structured | SUPER type + PartiQL; array functions (nine new, Mar 2026 ✓ WN) |
| Modeling | star schema (fact + dimensions) for BI; denormalise to avoid joins; MVs for repeated aggregates |
Red flags: DISTSTYLE ALL on huge tables; KEY on a skewed column; unsorted regions → VACUUM/auto; many tiny INSERTs.

### DynamoDB ✓ [DDB quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/ServiceQuotas.html)
- **Model from access patterns**. Partition key = high cardinality, evenly requested; sort key enables range queries/one-to-many; **single-table design** (entity type prefixes) reduces round trips.
- **GSI** (any attributes as keys, eventually consistent, own capacity, add anytime; ≤ 20 default ✓) vs **LSI** (same partition key, alternate sort key, strong reads, **created at table creation only**, 10 GB per item collection, ≤ 5 ✓). Sparse indexes (only items with the attribute). Project only needed attributes (≤ 100 projected non-key attributes ✓).
- Hot partitions: better keys; **write sharding** (random/calculated suffix); on-demand; adaptive capacity ~; burst. Inverted index via GSI (swap PK/SK).
- Access pattern example: orders by customer newest-first → PK `customerId`, SK `orderDate`; by order ID → GSI PK `orderId`; by status across customers → GSI PK `status`, SK `orderDate`. (An LSI cannot do this: shares `customerId`.)

### Lake Formation / lake tables
Databases/tables in the Glue Data Catalog on S3; partition on filter columns (date, region); columnar + compression; LF-tags on databases/tables/columns for governance; table formats (Iceberg) for evolution; layers raw → curated → consumption.

## 2. Changes to data characteristics (2.4.2)
Volume growth (partition/compaction, scale-out), velocity change (batch → stream), **variety/drift** (new columns, type changes, nested JSON), cardinality shifts (hot keys), data skew. Techniques: schema-on-read, Glue DynamicFrame `ResolveChoice`, Schema Registry compatibility modes, Iceberg schema/partition evolution (no rewrite), crawler policy Log, defensive parsing, backfills with idempotent jobs, monitoring DQ rules, alerts on schema drift.
- Athena/Parquet: **adding a trailing column** is compatible (old files → NULL); renaming/reordering depends on by-name vs by-position mapping ~.
- Avro: forward/backward/full compatibility (Schema Registry) ~.

## 3. Schema conversion (2.4.3) ✓ [DMS Schema Conversion](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_SchemaConversion.html)
- **DMS Schema Conversion** = managed feature of AWS DMS that converts **schemas (not data)** from source engines to Aurora/RDS/Redshift targets; builds on the **AWS SCT** conversion engine (SCT itself was removed from the in-scope list ✓ but skill 2.4.3 still names it). Resources: **instance profile** (network/security), **data providers** (source/target), **migration project** (+ Secrets Manager secrets). Workflow: assess (assessment report shows what converts automatically vs manual) → convert → review/edit → apply to target or export SQL to S3. **Generative AI conversion** for hard objects on some paths (Oracle/SQL Server/Db2/SAP ASE → PostgreSQL). Extension packs emulate missing source features.
- Supported (examples ✓): Oracle → Aurora/RDS PostgreSQL, MySQL, **Redshift**; SQL Server → PostgreSQL/MySQL; PostgreSQL → MySQL; MySQL → PostgreSQL; Db2 LUW/z/OS → PostgreSQL; SAP ASE → PostgreSQL.
- Pair with **DMS data migration** (full load + CDC) — conversion first, then data.

## 4. Lineage (2.4.4)
- **SageMaker Catalog lineage** (OpenLineage-compatible ~): graph of datasets, jobs, runs across projects; **SageMaker ML Lineage Tracking**: tracks ML workflow artifacts (datasets, training jobs, models, endpoints) ✓ (named in guide). Glue/EMR/Airflow can emit lineage events ~. Use for impact analysis, audit, debugging.
- Not lineage tools: CloudTrail (API calls), Config (resource state), Glue crawler (schema).

## 5. Indexing, partitioning, compression, optimisation (2.4.5)
| Topic | Practice |
|---|---|
| Partitioning (lake) | by common filters, moderate cardinality; avoid minute/user_id partitions; Athena ≤1 M partitions/scan ✓; Hive-style `k=v` prefixes; partition projection |
| File layout | 128 MB–1 GB columnar files; compaction; avoid small files (S3 req limits ✓) |
| Compression | Snappy default for Parquet; ZSTD better ratio; gzip not splittable; BZIP2 slow |
| Redshift | sort/dist keys; MVs; ANALYZE/VACUUM (auto); compression encodings |
| DynamoDB | key design, GSIs, projections, TTL |
| RDS/Aurora | B-tree indexes, composite/covering indexes, partitioned tables, `EXPLAIN` ~; pgvector HNSW/IVF for vectors |
| OpenSearch | shards/replicas, ISM lifecycle ~ |
| Iceberg | hidden partitioning, sort order, compaction (`OPTIMIZE`), S3 Tables auto maintenance ✓ |

## 6. Vectorization (2.4.6 — NEW) and Bedrock Knowledge Bases
- **Vectorization** = turning text/images/audio into embeddings with an embedding model (e.g., Amazon Titan, Cohere Embed) so semantic similarity becomes vector distance. Pipeline: **ingest → chunk → embed → store (vector index) → retrieve top-K → augment prompt (RAG)**. Chunking strategy (size/overlap), metadata filters, re-embedding on model change (dimension must match index).
- **Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases** ✓ automates ingestion from S3: "converts unstructured text to chunks and vectors and stores it in a PostgreSQL database" when Aurora is the vector store ✓; other stores: OpenSearch (Serverless), S3 Vectors ~, etc.; queried by agents/RetrieveAndGenerate APIs ~.
- Dimension examples ✓: Titan v2 256/512/1024; Titan multimodal 1,536; Cohere Embed 1,024. DynamoDB vector index max 4,096 dims ✓.
- Choose: managed pipeline → Knowledge Bases; custom → Lambda/Glue calling Bedrock embeddings into pgvector/OpenSearch/MemoryDB; high recall → HNSW; cheap/low memory → IVF (see 2.1 §9).

## 7. Worked scenarios
1. *Redshift orders (2 B) ⋈ customers (500 M) on customer_id* → **DISTKEY(customer_id) both** (ALL on 500 M rows is wrong).
2. *Queries by customer newest-first and by order ID* → PK customerId / SK orderDate + **GSI on orderId** (LSI can't).
3. *Oracle → Aurora PostgreSQL, minimal downtime* → **DMS Schema Conversion** then **DMS full load + CDC**.
4. *New optional Parquet column; old partitions must keep working* → add column to table definition; old files return NULL.
5. *Upstream int → string* → **ResolveChoice** + schema registry/catalog versioning.
6. *RAG over S3 documents with minimal code* → **Bedrock Knowledge Bases**.

## 8. Keyword → answer and traps
| Keyword | Answer | Trap |
|---|---|---|
| co-locate join | KEY dist | ALL on big table |
| small dimension | ALL | KEY |
| range filter on date | sort key date | interleaved all columns |
| query by non-key attribute across partitions | GSI | LSI / Scan |
| hot DynamoDB key | write sharding | DAX (read cache) |
| heterogeneous DB migration | DMS Schema Conversion + DMS | DataSync |
| data lineage across projects | SageMaker Catalog | CloudTrail |
| too many partitions/small files | coarser partitions + compaction | more partition columns |
| vector recall vs memory | HNSW vs IVF | B-tree/GIN |

# Task 3.1 — Automate data processing by using AWS services (Domain 3 = 22 %)
Tags: ✓ verified 2026-10-20 (link) · ~ established, not re-fetched. Skills 3.1.1–3.1.9. Orchestration detail lives in D1 `1.3-orchestration.md`; this file is the *operate/troubleshoot/automate* view.

## 0. Skill map
3.1.1 orchestrate (MWAA/SFN) §1 · 3.1.2 troubleshoot managed workflows §2 · 3.1.3 SDKs §3 · 3.1.4 service features (EMR/Redshift/Glue) §4 · 3.1.5 data APIs §5 · 3.1.6 prepare data §6 · 3.1.7 query (Athena) §7 · 3.1.8 Lambda automation §8 · 3.1.9 events/schedulers §9

## 1. Orchestrate pipelines (3.1.1)
- **Step Functions**: Standard ≤ 1 y / 25,000 history events / history kept 90 d ✓; Express ≤ 5 min ✓; `.sync` and `.waitForTaskToken` patterns; Distributed Map for large fan-out ✓.
- **MWAA** ✓: environment classes mw1.micro → 2xlarge; DAG files in S3; schedulers 2–5; deferrable operators.
- Pick: serverless AWS-native → SFN; existing Airflow → MWAA; Glue-only → Glue workflows. (see D1 §1.3)

## 2. Troubleshoot Amazon managed workflows (3.1.2)
| Symptom | Where to look | Typical cause / fix |
|---|---|---|
| **MWAA** DAG not listed | Scheduler / DAG processing logs (CloudWatch) | import/syntax error; wrong `dags/` path; DAG file parse timeout |
| MWAA plugin/requirements fail | Worker/scheduler logs; env status "update failed" | pip needs internet → NAT or VPC endpoints/private repo; version constraints |
| MWAA tasks queued, not running | metrics (queued tasks), worker count | environment class too small; raise max workers; `celery.worker_autoscale`; pool slots |
| MWAA task fails AccessDenied | task log | execution role lacks Glue/S3/KMS permission |
| **Step Functions** execution failed | console graph + execution history/CloudWatch Logs | task error in a state; `States.TaskFailed`, `States.Timeout`; Retry/Catch missing; IAM role for state machine; payload > 256 KiB ✓ |
| SFN history limit | `ExecutionFailed` – history > 25,000 events ✓ | Distributed Map / child executions |
| SFN throttled | `ExecutionThrottled` metric | state-transition / StartExecution quota ✓ |
| **Glue workflow** stuck | workflow run graph | upstream crawler failed; trigger condition not met |
| **EventBridge** target not invoked | rule metrics (`FailedInvocations`), DLQ | target permission/resource policy; pattern mismatch |
Always: CloudWatch Logs + metrics, enable logging on state machines, set alarms (SFN `ExecutionsFailed`, `ExecutionsTimedOut`), EventBridge rule on status change → SNS.

## 3. Calling SDKs from code (3.1.3)
Use boto3/AWS SDKs to start Glue jobs, run Athena queries, call Bedrock, put Kinesis records, etc. Concepts the exam tests: **paginators** (list calls return ≤ 1,000 S3 keys per page), **waiters**, **retries with backoff** (standard/adaptive modes), credentials via IAM roles (not keys), Region config, async polling for Athena (`start_query_execution` → `get_query_execution` → `get_query_results`), batch APIs (`put_records` ≤ 500 ✓, `batch_write_item` ≤ 25 ~), idempotency tokens (`ClientRequestToken`), Redshift Data API (no persistent connection; async SQL over HTTPS) ~.
```python
import boto3
s3 = boto3.client("s3")
for page in s3.get_paginator("list_objects_v2").paginate(Bucket="lake", Prefix="raw/"):
    for o in page.get("Contents", []): ...
```

## 4. Using service features to process data (3.1.4)
- **Glue**: job bookmarks, auto scaling, Flex ✓, workflows, DQ, DynamicFrames, Spark UI, observability metrics ✓.
- **EMR**: managed scaling, instance fleets/Spot, steps, bootstrap actions, EMRFS, security configurations, log archival to S3, EMR Serverless/on-EKS.
- **Redshift**: COPY/UNLOAD, MVs (auto-refresh), stored procedures, scheduled queries (query editor v2 ~), Data API, concurrency scaling/WLM, Spectrum, federated queries, streaming ingestion ✓, zero-ETL.
- **Athena**: CTAS, views, workgroups, partition projection, federated queries, Spark notebooks, capacity reservations ✓.

## 5. Consume and maintain data APIs (3.1.5)
API Gateway (REST/HTTP) in front of Lambda/DynamoDB/Athena; **maintain**: throttling & usage plans, API keys, authorizers (IAM, Cognito, Lambda), stages/canary releases, caching, request validation, CloudWatch metrics/logs/access logs, versioning/deprecation, WAF for abuse ✓ (in scope). Consuming external APIs: handle pagination/rate limits/retries; store credentials in Secrets Manager.

## 6. Prepare data for transformation (3.1.6)
- **Glue DataBrew**: visual profiling, 250+ transforms ~, **recipes** reusable on new data, jobs write to S3/catalog, data quality rulesets, sampling.
- **Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio** (NEW in v1.1 wording): integrated workspace (notebooks/JupyterLab, SQL editor, visual ETL, Glue/EMR/Athena/Redshift compute) inside a *project*; governed via SageMaker Catalog; choose it when data engineers and scientists collaborate under a governed domain.
- **SageMaker Data Wrangler**: visual data prep in notebooks (skill 3.2.2). **Jupyter/Athena notebooks** for exploration. **Lambda** for light cleaning.

## 7. Query data with Athena (3.1.7)
✓ [Athena capacity](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/capacity-management.html): **capacity reservations** = dedicated serverless DPUs (1 DPU ≈ 4 vCPU/16 GB); min **4 DPUs**; reservation creation can take up to 30 min; queries on reserved capacity **don't count toward DML/DDL quotas**; queued up to **10 hours**; up to 20 workgroups per reservation, 100 reservations / 1,000 DPUs per account/Region; DML uses 4–124 DPUs per query (DDL 4); Spark-enabled workgroups not supported. Per-query billing (per TB scanned) and reservations can coexist. Query string ≤ 262,144 bytes; ≤ 1 M partitions scanned ✓.
Cost/limit control via **workgroups** ~: per-query data-scanned cutoff, workgroup-wide periodic limit with SNS alarm, enforced result location + encryption, CloudWatch metrics, tags for cost allocation, engine version pinning.
Tune: Parquet/ORC, partitioning/projection, compression, CTAS compaction, `LIMIT`, column selection, avoid many small files, result reuse for repeated queries.

## 8. Lambda to automate processing (3.1.8)
Triggers: S3 events, SQS (set max concurrency), Kinesis/DynamoDB Streams (ParallelizationFactor ✓), EventBridge/Scheduler, API Gateway, SNS, Firehose transform. Patterns: validate-and-quarantine uploads, start Glue/Step Functions, enrich/notify, tag/move files, trigger crawlers. Constraints ✓: 15 min, 6 MB sync payload, 10,240 MB, concurrency 1,000; make handlers idempotent; use DLQ/on-failure destination.

## 9. Manage events and schedulers (3.1.9)
EventBridge **rules** (event patterns, cron/rate in UTC ~), **Scheduler** ✓ (time zones ~, one-time, flexible windows, retries, DLQ-like retention, universal targets), **Pipes** (source → filter → enrich → target), **Archive/replay**, API destinations, event buses (custom/partner/cross-account). Monitor with `Invocations`, `FailedInvocations`, DLQ; least-privilege target roles.

## 10. Worked scenarios
1. *New Airflow DAG file isn't visible* → DAG-processing logs for import errors + check `dags/` path.
2. *Standard workflow with 60,000-item inline Map fails at 25,000 events* → **Distributed Map** ✓.
3. *Athena DML queue exceptions during business hours, predictable workload* → **capacity reservation** + workgroup assignment ✓.
4. *Every upload validated, bad files quarantined* → S3 event → Lambda → move to `quarantine/`.
5. *Data engineers + scientists need a governed shared workspace* → SageMaker Unified Studio project.

## 11. Keyword → answer and traps
| Keyword | Answer | Trap |
|---|---|---|
| DAG missing in MWAA | DAG processing log | VPC route tables |
| more than 1,000 S3 keys | paginator | MaxKeys > 1000 |
| predictable heavy Athena load | capacity reservation | bigger workgroup |
| cap per-query Athena cost | workgroup per-query data limit | query timeout |
| time-zone-aware schedule | EventBridge Scheduler | rule cron |
| no-code reusable cleaning | DataBrew recipe | Lambda |
| API abuse by few clients | API Gateway throttling + usage plans | more Lambda memory |

<!-- source: guide/D3-operations-support/3.2-analysis.md -->

# Task 3.2 — Analyze data by using AWS services (D3)
Tags: ✓ verified 2026-10-20 (link) · ~ established, not re-fetched. Skills 3.2.1–3.2.6.

## 1. Visualise (3.2.1)
| Tool | Role |
|---|---|
| **Amazon Quick (formerly QuickSight; "Quick Suite" family)** | BI dashboards, analyses, embedding, ML insights; **SPICE** in-memory import with scheduled refresh vs **direct query**; **row-level security** via permissions dataset, column-level security; sources: Athena, Redshift, S3, RDS, Aurora, OpenSearch… |
| **DataBrew** | visual profiling (distributions, correlations, missing values, outliers) |
| **Managed Grafana** (in scope ✓) | operational/time-series dashboards (CloudWatch, OpenSearch, Athena sources) |
| **CloudWatch dashboards** | pipeline metrics |
| **OpenSearch Dashboards** | log/search analytics |
Choose: slow/expensive dashboard on data that changes daily → **SPICE + scheduled refresh**; near-real-time freshness → **direct query** (to a fast engine such as Redshift); per-user row filtering → **row-level security**; public embedding → anonymous embedding / capacity pricing ~.

## 2. Verify and clean data (3.2.2)
- **Lambda** (light validation/quarantine), **Athena** (profiling SQL: duplicates `GROUP BY … HAVING COUNT(*)>1`, nulls `COUNT_IF(col IS NULL)`, ranges, `approx_distinct`), **Quick** (visual checks), **Jupyter / Athena Spark notebooks / SageMaker Unified Studio**, **SageMaker Data Wrangler** (visual prep), **DataBrew** (recipes), Glue Data Quality (see 3.4).
- Typical cleaning: deduplicate (`ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY key ORDER BY ts DESC)=1`), standardise types/dates, trim/case, handle nulls (impute/drop/flag), outlier rules, reference-data lookups, PII masking.

## 3. SQL in Redshift and Athena (3.2.3 — wording changed in v1.1)
- Both: ANSI-ish SQL, CTEs, window functions, views. **Athena** (Trino/Presto-based): views stored in the Glue Data Catalog; CTAS; `UNNEST` arrays; `TABLESAMPLE` ~; Iceberg DML ~. **Redshift** (PostgreSQL-derived): views, **late-binding views** (reference external tables), **materialized views**, SUPER/PartiQL with array functions (new Mar 2026 ✓), stored procedures, `MERGE`.
- Views vs MV vs CTAS: view = stored query (no data); MV = stored result (refresh); CTAS = materialised table (static).
```sql
-- view (Athena or Redshift)
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW active_customers AS SELECT * FROM customers WHERE status = 'ACTIVE';
```

## 4. Athena notebooks with Apache Spark (3.2.4)
Serverless interactive PySpark/Spark SQL on S3 and the Glue Data Catalog; no cluster to manage; sessions with DPUs; good for exploration, ad hoc transformations, charting; **not supported on capacity reservations** (Spark workgroups excluded ✓). Alternative: EMR Studio, SageMaker Unified Studio notebooks, Glue interactive sessions.

## 5. Provisioned vs serverless trade-offs (3.2.5)
| Dimension | Serverless (Athena, Glue, EMR Serverless, Redshift Serverless, Lambda, Aurora Serverless v2, DynamoDB on-demand) | Provisioned (Redshift RA3, EMR on EC2, Athena capacity reservation, DynamoDB provisioned, Aurora/RDS) |
|---|---|---|
| Ops | none/low | capacity planning, patching windows |
| Cost | pay per use, cheap for spiky/idle; higher unit price at steady 24/7 | cheaper at predictable high utilisation; reservations/Savings Plans (Redshift Serverless 3-yr up to 45 % ✓) |
| Performance | scales automatically; cold-start/queueing variance | predictable, tunable, dedicated |
| Control | limited tuning | full (instance types, WLM, networking) |
| Quotas | account concurrency (Athena DML queue ✓) | reserved DPUs/nodes |
Hybrid example ✓: Athena on-demand for ad hoc + **capacity reservation** for predictable critical workgroups (does not consume DML quota; queue ≤ 10 h; min 4 DPUs).
Rules: unpredictable/dev/test → serverless; steady heavy → provisioned + reservations; peaks over steady base → provisioned + concurrency scaling.

## 6. Aggregation, rolling average, grouping, pivoting (3.2.6)
```sql
-- grouping and subtotals
SELECT region, product, SUM(amount) FROM sales GROUP BY ROLLUP (region, product);
-- 7-day rolling average per store
SELECT store, day, AVG(daily_sales) OVER (PARTITION BY store ORDER BY day ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS rolling7 FROM store_sales;
-- running total / rank / lag
SELECT *, SUM(x) OVER (PARTITION BY k ORDER BY d) AS running, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY k ORDER BY x DESC) AS rnk, LAG(x) OVER (PARTITION BY k ORDER BY d) AS prev FROM t;
-- pivot via conditional aggregation (portable)
SELECT store, SUM(CASE WHEN q = 'Q1' THEN amt END) AS q1, SUM(CASE WHEN q = 'Q2' THEN amt END) AS q2 FROM s GROUP BY store;
-- percentiles / approximations
SELECT approx_percentile(latency_ms, 0.95) FROM requests;   -- Athena
```
Terms: **aggregation** (SUM/COUNT/AVG over groups), **grouping sets/ROLLUP/CUBE**, **window frame** (`ROWS` vs `RANGE`, preceding/following), **rolling average** (fixed-size window), **pivot** (rows → columns; Redshift has `PIVOT`/`UNPIVOT`; Athena uses conditional aggregation or `map_agg`), **time bucketing** (`date_trunc`).

## 7. Worked scenarios
1. *Dashboard slow/expensive; data updates daily* → Quick **SPICE** import + daily refresh.
2. *Rolling 7-day average per store in Athena* → window frame `ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW`.
3. *Data scientist wants interactive PySpark on S3, no clusters* → **Athena Spark notebook**.
4. *Dev team with intermittent Redshift queries* → **Redshift Serverless**.
5. *Per-salesperson regional rows in dashboards* → **row-level security**.

## 8. Keyword → answer and traps
| Keyword | Answer | Trap |
|---|---|---|
| fast dashboard, daily data | SPICE | direct query to Athena |
| per-user row filtering | RLS permissions dataset | separate dashboards |
| rolling average | window frame ROWS … 6 PRECEDING | GROUP BY |
| find duplicates | GROUP BY … HAVING COUNT>1 | SELECT DISTINCT |
| unpredictable/idle workload | serverless | provisioned 24/7 |
| steady heavy workload | provisioned + reservation | on-demand |
| PySpark without cluster | Athena notebooks | EMR cluster |

<!-- source: guide/D3-operations-support/3.3-monitoring.md -->

# Task 3.3 — Maintain and monitor data pipelines (D3)
Tags: ✓ verified 2026-10-20 (link) · ~ established, not re-fetched. Skills 3.3.1–3.3.8 (overlaps D4 4.4).

## 1. Observability toolbox (which tool answers which question)
| Question | Tool |
|---|---|
| Is it healthy / how much / how fast? | **CloudWatch metrics** + alarms + dashboards (Glue job metrics, Kinesis `IteratorAge`, Redshift `PercentageDiskSpaceUsed`, SQS depth, Lambda throttles) |
| What did the app print? | **CloudWatch Logs** (log groups, retention, metric filters, subscription filters) |
| Who called which API? | **CloudTrail** (management events default; **data events** opt-in; **CloudTrail Lake** SQL; Insights for anomalies) |
| What changed in configuration / is it compliant? | **AWS Config** (rules, timeline, conformance packs) |
| Why did the Spark job slow down? | **Spark UI / history server**, Glue job run insights/observability metrics ✓, EMR logs on S3 / YARN UI |
| Workflow state | Step Functions execution history (90 d ✓), MWAA task logs, Glue workflow graph |
| Event → action | **EventBridge** rules (Glue/EMR/DMS/SFN/Redshift state changes) → SNS/Lambda/SQS |
| Cost | Cost Explorer, Budgets (in scope ✓), cost allocation tags |

## 2. Logging and monitoring for audit and traceability (3.3.2, 3.3.7)
- **CloudWatch Logs**: structured JSON logs; retention policy; encryption with KMS; metric filters (turn "ERROR" lines into metrics); subscription filters → Kinesis/Firehose/Lambda/OpenSearch; export to S3; **log classes** (Standard vs Infrequent Access ~); cross-account observability ✓ (monitoring account can query source accounts).
- Enable service logs: Glue **continuous logging** + Spark UI ✓, EMR log URI, Redshift **audit logging** (connection, user, user-activity logs to S3/CloudWatch), S3 server access logs/CloudTrail data events, VPC Flow Logs, Lambda logs, API Gateway access logs, Step Functions logging, MWAA component logs, Athena workgroup metrics.
- Traceability: correlation IDs in logs, lineage (SageMaker Catalog), CloudTrail for control plane, immutable log storage (S3 Object Lock ~), log file integrity validation (CloudTrail).

## 3. Extract logs for audits (3.3.1)
Methods: CloudWatch Logs **export task** to S3; **subscription filter → Firehose → S3** (continuous); CloudTrail trail to S3 (+ **Lake** event data store for SQL); S3 server access logs; Config snapshots to S3; Athena over logs (CloudTrail table with partition projection); Logs Insights for ad hoc.

## 4. Alerts (3.3.3)
CloudWatch alarm (static or anomaly detection ~) → **SNS** (email/SMS/HTTP/Lambda) → on-call; composite alarms; EventBridge rules on failure events → SNS; Step Functions Catch → SNS publish; Glue job **delay notification threshold** ✓; DMS event subscriptions; Redshift event notifications; budget alerts. SQS DLQ depth alarm for poison messages.

## 5. Troubleshoot performance (3.3.4) — symptom → cause → fix
| Service | Symptom | Cause / fix |
|---|---|---|
| Kinesis | `WriteProvisionedThroughputExceeded` | hot shard/too few shards → better key, more shards/on-demand, batch (PutRecords ≤500 ✓), KPL, backoff |
| Kinesis | rising `GetRecords.IteratorAgeMilliseconds` | slow consumer → ParallelizationFactor ≤10 ✓, EFO, more shards, faster code |
| Lambda | throttles / 429 | concurrency 1,000 ✓ default → reserved/provisioned, quota, SQS buffer |
| Lambda | timeout | 15 min ✓ → Glue/Fargate; raise memory (CPU) |
| S3 | 503 Slow Down | > 3,500/5,500 req/s/prefix ✓ → prefixes, fewer small files, backoff |
| Glue | OOM / skew | salting, repartition, larger/R.* workers ✓, AQE |
| Glue | slow listing | small files → `groupFiles`, compaction |
| Glue | reprocessing | bookmarks off / `job.commit()` missing |
| Redshift | queue waits | automatic WLM, concurrency scaling, SQA, query priorities |
| Redshift | slow joins | wrong DIST key (DS_BCAST/DS_DIST), stale stats, no sort key |
| Redshift | locks | `STV_LOCKS`/`SVV_TRANSACTIONS`, `PG_TERMINATE_BACKEND` |
| Redshift | disk full | skew, large temp, resize/RA3, vacuum, drop unused |
| Athena | slow/expensive | Parquet + partition + compaction; `TooManyRequestsException` → capacity reservation ✓ |
| EMR | job slow / Spot loss | instance fleets, task-node Spot only, managed scaling, YARN memory config |
| DynamoDB | throttling | on-demand/auto scaling, key design, adaptive capacity |
| RDS | CPU/connections | RDS Proxy, replicas, Performance Insights ~ |
| MSK | broker CPU/disk, consumer lag | scale brokers/storage, partitions ≥ consumers, `ConsumerLag` metrics ~ |
| OpenSearch | red/yellow cluster, JVM pressure | shards sizing, replicas, storage/instance scale, UltraWarm/cold ~ |

## 6. CloudTrail (3.3.5) — also D4 4.4
Management events (control plane: CreateJob, PutBucketPolicy, DisableKey) recorded by default (90-day Event history, free) ~; **data events** (S3 object-level `GetObject/PutObject/DeleteObject`, Lambda invoke, DynamoDB item ops) are **opt-in** — answer for "who deleted this object". **Insights** detect unusual API volume. **Trails** → S3 (+CloudWatch Logs, SNS); org trails; log file validation (digest). **CloudTrail Lake**: managed event data store, SQL queries, org-wide. Use EventBridge rules on CloudTrail events for real-time alerts (e.g., `DisableKey`, `ScheduleKeyDeletion`).

## 7. Troubleshoot and maintain pipelines — Glue and EMR (3.3.6)
- **Glue**: job run status/error (CloudWatch error log group), continuous logging, job metrics (`glue.driver.jvm.heap.usage`, shuffle, DPU use) ✓, **Spark UI** needs enabled + logs path ✓, retries 0–10 ✓, timeout ✓, `--additional-python-modules` for missing libs, VPC connection (SG self-reference, NAT/endpoints), AccessDenied on S3/KMS/catalog → role, **max concurrency 1** ✓ causing "concurrent runs exceeded" → raise or queue.
- **EMR**: cluster/step state, `stderr/stdout/syslog` + YARN container logs in log URI S3 bucket ✓ (enable *before* failure), Spot interruptions, bootstrap failures, memory (`spark.executor.memory`, overhead), HDFS capacity (core nodes), security group/subnet issues, EMR Serverless job logs, release support windows ✓ (5.36 and 6.6–6.15 extended through 2027-06-30; 7.0–7.10 through 2027-08-31).
- Maintain: patching/upgrade windows, version upgrades (Glue 5.1 default ✓, 6.0 available ✓), dependency pinning, runbooks, alarms on SLAs, DLQs, tests.

## 8. CloudWatch Logs Insights (3.3.7, 3.3.8) ✓ [Logs Insights](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/AnalyzingLogData.html)
- Interactive queries across log groups; **three languages**: Logs Insights QL, **OpenSearch PPL**, **OpenSearch SQL** ✓; limits: **100 concurrent** Insights QL queries per account (15 for PPL/SQL), **60-minute** timeout, results kept **7 days**; billed per **uncompressed GB scanned** ✓; automatic field discovery for Lambda, CloudTrail, VPC, Route 53 logs and JSON logs; **field indexes** reduce scan cost/time; pattern detection; saved queries; cross-account (monitoring account).
```
fields @timestamp, @message
| filter @message like /ERROR/
| stats count(*) as errors by bin(5m)
| sort errors desc
```
- **Analyze logs with**: Logs Insights (recent, ad hoc), **Athena** (S3-resident logs: CloudTrail, ALB, VPC Flow, S3 access, Firehose-delivered CloudWatch logs; cheap, SQL), **OpenSearch Service** (near-real-time search + dashboards, ingest via subscription filter/Firehose), **EMR/Glue Spark** (very large "big data application logs", parsing/enrichment), Managed Grafana for dashboards.
- Pick: seconds-old search + dashboards → OpenSearch; occasional audit SQL on archived logs → Athena; quick troubleshooting on live logs → Logs Insights; 50 TB/day parsing → Spark on EMR/Glue (D4 4.4.5).

## 9. Worked scenarios
1. *Alert when a Kinesis consumer falls behind* → alarm on `GetRecords.IteratorAgeMilliseconds` → SNS.
2. *Email on any Glue job failure/timeout* → EventBridge rule on Glue Job State Change → SNS.
3. *More than 5 ERROR lines in 5 min* → CloudWatch Logs **metric filter** + alarm.
4. *Who deleted objects from the bucket?* → CloudTrail **S3 data events** (write) on that bucket.
5. *EMR step failed and cluster terminated; no logs* → configure **log URI** (S3) at launch.
6. *Searchable app logs in seconds with dashboards* → CloudWatch Logs → Firehose → **OpenSearch**.

## 10. Keyword → answer and traps
| Keyword | Answer | Trap |
|---|---|---|
| who did what (API) | CloudTrail | CloudWatch |
| object-level deletes | S3 data events | management events |
| resource configuration history | Config | CloudTrail |
| lag / consumer behind | IteratorAge | IncomingBytes |
| ad hoc log query now | Logs Insights | Athena |
| archived logs SQL | Athena over S3 | EMR cluster |
| near-real-time log search | OpenSearch | Athena |
| log lines → metric/alarm | metric filter | CloudTrail |

<!-- source: guide/D3-operations-support/3.4-data-quality.md -->

# Task 3.4 — Ensure data quality (D3)
Tags: ✓ verified 2026-10-20 (link) · ~ established, not re-fetched. Skills 3.4.1–3.4.5.

## 1. Dimensions of data quality (use these words in answers)
Completeness (no unexpected nulls) · Uniqueness (no duplicates) · Validity (format/range/domain) · Accuracy · Consistency (across systems/time) · Timeliness/freshness · Integrity (referential) · Volume/row-count anomalies · Schema conformance.

## 2. Quality checks while processing (3.4.1)
Where to check: at **ingest** (Lambda/S3-event validation, Firehose transform, Glue crawler classification), **in transform** (Glue Data Quality, Deequ on Spark/EMR, DataBrew), **before publish** (gate in Step Functions Choice), **after load** (Redshift/Athena SQL assertions, DMS validation ~).
Actions on failure: fail the job; quarantine bad rows to a `rejected/` prefix; continue but alert; route record to DLQ; block downstream steps.

## 3. AWS Glue Data Quality and DQDL (3.4.2) ✓ [DQDL](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/dqdl.html)
- **DQDL** = case-sensitive language; a ruleset is `Rules = [ … ]` (capital R); rule shape `<RuleType> <Parameter> <Expression>`.
- **Rule types ✓**: `ColumnExists`, `ColumnCount`, `ColumnDataType`, `ColumnLength`, `ColumnNamesMatchPattern`, `ColumnValues`, `Completeness`, `IsComplete`, `IsUnique`, `IsPrimaryKey`, `Uniqueness`, `UniqueValueRatio`, `DistinctValuesCount`, `Mean`, `Sum`, `StandardDeviation`, `Entropy`, `ColumnCorrelation`, `RowCount`, `RowCountMatch`, `DatasetMatch`, `AggregateMatch`, `ReferentialIntegrity`, `SchemaMatch`, `DataFreshness`, `CustomSql`, `Distribution`, `DetectAnomalies`, and file-based `FileFreshness/FileMatch/FileUniqueness/FileSize`.
- **Expressions ✓**: `=`, `!=`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`, `between x and y`, `in [..]`, `not in`, `matches /regex/`, `now()` for dates, **`with threshold`** (percentage of values satisfying; only ColumnValues/ColumnDataType/CustomSql), keywords `NULL`, `EMPTY`, `WHITESPACES_ONLY`.
- **Composite rules**: `(rule1) and (rule2)` / `or` — evaluated per rule over the whole dataset by default; set `compositeRuleEvaluation.method=ROW` for row-wise evaluation ✓.
- **`where` clause** (Glue 4.0 ✓) filters rows for conditional rules; **dynamic rules** compare with history: `RowCount > avg(last(3))` (Glue ETL only ✓); **analyzers** gather statistics without pass/fail; **labels** (≤10 per rule) for reporting.
- Example ruleset:
```
Rules = [
  IsComplete "order_id", IsUnique "order_id",
  ColumnValues "status" in ["NEW","PAID","SHIPPED"],
  Completeness "customer_id" > 0.98,
  ColumnValues "email" matches "[a-zA-Z0-9._%+-]+@[a-zA-Z0-9.-]+" with threshold > 0.95,
  RowCount > avg(last(3)) * 0.8,
  DataFreshness "event_ts" <= 24 hours
]
```
- Run: **Evaluate Data Quality** node in Glue Studio / `EvaluateDataQuality` transform in ETL (can **fail the job**, publish to CloudWatch, output row-level results to isolate bad rows) or evaluate rulesets on **Data Catalog tables** (scheduled, no ETL). Row-level pass/fail columns (`DataQualityRulesPass/Fail`) allow quarantine of failing rows ✓.
- Recommendations: Glue can **recommend** rules from profiling; **anomaly detection** (`DetectAnomalies`) for drift ~.

## 4. Other quality tools
- **DataBrew** ✓ (guide names): profile jobs (stats, correlations), **data quality rulesets** (column/row checks, thresholds), recipes to fix, results to S3; no code.
- **Deequ / PyDeequ** (open-source on Spark; EMR/Glue) ~ — what Glue DQ builds on.
- **Athena/Redshift SQL assertions**, Great-Expectations-style frameworks (not AWS-native ✗).
- **DMS data validation** for source vs target row/column comparison ~.
- **Schema checks**: Glue Schema Registry compatibility, crawler Log policy, `SchemaMatch`.
- Alerting: DQ result → CloudWatch metric → alarm → SNS; EventBridge on Glue DQ result events ~.

## 5. Data consistency (3.4.3)
Compare counts/checksums/aggregates between layers (`RowCountMatch`, `DatasetMatch`, `AggregateMatch`), idempotent upserts (MERGE) to prevent drift, Iceberg ACID snapshots, DMS validation, referential integrity (`ReferentialIntegrity`), eventual consistency awareness (DynamoDB eventually vs strongly consistent reads; GSIs eventually consistent; S3 now strongly consistent ~), reconcile late/duplicate events with event-time + dedupe keys, DataBrew consistency profiling.

## 6. Data sampling techniques (3.4.4)
| Technique | Use |
|---|---|
| Simple random (with seed) | unbiased, reproducible profiling |
| **Stratified** | preserve proportions of segments/categories (rare classes) |
| Systematic (every n-th) | ordered data; beware periodicity |
| Cluster | sample whole groups (cheap for partitioned files) |
| Reservoir | fixed-size sample from a stream of unknown length |
| Head/first-N | biased — avoid for quality conclusions |
Tools: DataBrew sample size settings, Athena `TABLESAMPLE` ~ / `ORDER BY rand() LIMIT`, Spark `sample()/sampleBy()`, Glue DQ on partitions. Sampling trades certainty for cost: profile a representative sample, run full-dataset *rules* for hard constraints.

## 7. Data skew mechanisms (3.4.5)
Skew = uneven key distribution → straggler tasks, OOM, hot shards/partitions. Detect: Spark UI task-time/size spread, Glue metrics, Redshift `SVV_TABLE_INFO.skew_rows` ~, DynamoDB hot key metrics/Contributor Insights ~, Kinesis hot shard. Mitigate:
| Where | Technique |
|---|---|
| Spark/Glue/EMR | **salting** hot keys (key + random salt, two-stage aggregate), `repartition` on better keys, **broadcast join** small side, AQE skew-join handling ~, filter/handle nulls & default keys separately |
| Redshift | choose higher-cardinality DISTKEY; use EVEN/AUTO if no good key |
| DynamoDB | high-cardinality partition key; **write sharding**; on-demand |
| Kinesis/MSK | distribute partition keys; more shards/partitions |
| Athena | avoid skewed partitions; bucket/compact |

## 8. Worked scenarios
1. *Stop publishing when > 5 % of order_id are null* → **Evaluate Data Quality** with `Completeness "order_id" > 0.95`, job set to fail on ruleset failure.
2. *Email must match pattern, no code, every new file* → **DataBrew ruleset** (or Glue DQ rule with `matches … with threshold`).
3. *Profile a 5 TB dataset cheaply but representative per segment* → **stratified + random sampling**.
4. *One customer holds 60 % of rows; executors OOM* → **salting**.
5. *Rows must be separated rather than failing whole job* → row-level DQ results → write failing rows to `rejected/`.

## 9. Keyword → answer and traps
| Keyword | Answer | Trap |
|---|---|---|
| rules language for Glue | DQDL | SQL only |
| stop pipeline on bad data | DQ with fail-job action | crawler |
| compare with previous runs | dynamic rule `last()` | static threshold |
| representative sample | stratified | first N rows |
| hot key OOM | salting / repartition | more workers |
| no-code rulesets | DataBrew | Lambda |
| source vs target equality | RowCountMatch / DMS validation | CloudTrail |

<!-- source: guide/D4-security-governance/4.1-authentication.md -->

# Task 4.1 — Apply authentication mechanisms (Domain 4 = 18 %)
Tags: ✓ verified 2026-10-20 (link) · ~ established, not re-fetched. Skills 4.1.1–4.1.7.

## 1. Network-level controls (4.1.1)
| Control | Facts |
|---|---|
| **Security group** | stateful, allow-only, attached to ENIs (Glue connections, Redshift, EMR, RDS, Lambda-in-VPC, interface endpoints); can reference other SGs; Glue needs a **self-referencing** inbound rule so its workers can talk to each other ~ |
| **NACL** | stateless, subnet-level, allow + deny, numbered rules |
| **VPC endpoints** | **Gateway** (S3, DynamoDB; free; route-table entry; endpoint policy) vs **Interface/PrivateLink** (most services: Kinesis, Glue, Athena, KMS, Secrets Manager, STS, Step Functions, Bedrock…; ENI + SG; hourly + per-GB cost) |
| NAT gateway | outbound internet from private subnets; fixed Elastic IP for partner allowlists; costs hourly + per-GB |
| Redshift | enhanced VPC routing forces COPY/UNLOAD traffic through VPC (endpoints/NAT) ~; publicly accessible = false; Firehose → Redshift requires publicly accessible cluster ✓ |
| Glue jobs in private subnet | S3 gateway endpoint (cheapest ✓), NAT/endpoints for other APIs |
Update security groups when: a job/ENI can't reach a database (open port from the job's SG), Lambda-in-VPC to RDS, MSK client access, Redshift from BI tool.

## 2. IAM groups, roles, endpoints, services (4.1.2, 4.1.4)
- **Principals**: users (avoid long-term keys), **groups** (permission bundles), **roles** (assumed; temporary credentials via STS). Prefer roles for services/workloads and **IAM Identity Center** for people ~.
- **Role anatomy**: *trust policy* (who can assume — e.g., `glue.amazonaws.com`, `lambda.amazonaws.com`, `states.amazonaws.com`, `redshift.amazonaws.com`, another account) + *permission policies* (what it can do). A Glue job role needs trust for Glue + S3/KMS/Catalog/Logs permissions; **`iam:PassRole`** is required for the identity that creates/starts the job.
- **Service roles for data services**: Lambda execution role (logs + source/target access), Glue job/crawler role, EMR service role + instance profile (EC2) + (EMR Serverless runtime role), Redshift role for COPY/UNLOAD/Spectrum (attach to cluster/namespace), Step Functions execution role (per-integration permissions), DMS (`dms-vpc-role`, endpoints roles) ~, Firehose delivery role, API Gateway execution/invocation role, CloudFormation service role (least-privilege deploys), CLI (profiles/SSO/assume-role) ✓ (4.1.4 names Lambda, API Gateway, CLI, CloudFormation).
- **Cross-account**: role in target account trusting the source account/role (then only the role's permissions apply) or resource policies (S3 bucket policy, KMS key policy, SQS/SNS policy, Lambda resource policy, Glue Data Catalog policy, Secrets Manager resource policy) + identity allow in source account.
- Guardrails: **permission boundaries** (max permissions of a role/user), **SCPs** (org-level deny/allow ceiling; never grant), session policies, conditions (`aws:SourceVpce`, `aws:PrincipalOrgID`, `aws:RequestedRegion`, `aws:SecureTransport`, tag keys).

## 3. IAM policies for endpoints and services (4.1.5)
- **VPC endpoint policy**: resource policy on an endpoint restricting what can be done through it (e.g., only the company's buckets) ✓ (topic-set Q49); combine with bucket policy `aws:SourceVpce` to force private path.
- **S3 Access Points**: per-application endpoints with their own policy (and VPC restriction), simplify shared-bucket permissions; **Multi-Region Access Points** ~; S3 Object Lambda ~.
- **PrivateLink**: interface endpoint to AWS services or your own endpoint service; security groups + endpoint policy; private DNS.
- Example (least-privilege S3 for a job):
```json
{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[
 {"Effect":"Allow","Action":"s3:GetObject","Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::lake/raw/*"},
 {"Effect":"Allow","Action":"s3:PutObject","Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::lake/curated/*"},
 {"Effect":"Allow","Action":"s3:ListBucket","Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::lake","Condition":{"StringLike":{"s3:prefix":["raw/*","curated/*"]}}}]}
```

## 4. Credentials: create and rotate (4.1.3) ✓ [Secrets Manager rotation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotating-secrets.html)
- **Secrets Manager**: store DB credentials/API keys; **automatic rotation** in two forms ✓: **managed rotation** (service-managed secrets, no Lambda) and **rotation by Lambda function** (other secret types; also managed external secrets for partners without Lambda ✓). Rotation updates the secret and the database/service; schedule in days; supports RDS, Aurora, Redshift, DocumentDB natively ~; cross-account via resource policy ~; KMS-encrypted; versions with staging labels (AWSCURRENT/AWSPENDING) ~.
- Use in data services: Glue connections, DMS endpoints, MSK SASL/SCRAM, Redshift (secret ARN for Data API/federated), Lambda env referencing the secret ARN (fetch at runtime; cache).
- No code changes needed if apps read the secret at runtime — answer to "rotate every 30 days without downtime" ✓ (mock Q17).
- Rotating **IAM access keys** (avoid: use roles); rotating **KMS** key material (4.3).

## 5. Managed vs unmanaged services (4.1.6)
Shared responsibility: with **managed** services (Glue, Athena, DynamoDB, Redshift Serverless, RDS, MSK Serverless) AWS secures/patches infrastructure and (for RDS) the OS and engine host; you manage data, identities, configuration, encryption settings, network exposure. With **unmanaged**/self-managed (Kafka on EC2, Spark on EC2, DB on EC2) you also patch OS, engines, HA, backups, scaling, encryption. Exam use: prefer managed for "least operational overhead", and know that "AWS patches RDS OS" ✓ vs "customer patches EC2 DB".

## 6. SageMaker Unified Studio domains, units, projects (4.1.7 — NEW) [secondary-verified]
- **Domain**: top-level boundary (organizational unit of governance): identity source (IAM Identity Center–based or IAM-based ~), blueprints/project profiles, default settings. Administrators manage users/groups and resources.
- **Domain units**: hierarchical grouping inside a domain (business units/teams) to delegate administration and policies ~.
- **Projects**: collaboration workspaces with members/roles, their own IAM role and resources (compute, storage, catalog assets); users "contribute to projects" ✓ (SMUS docs). Access to data flows through project membership and **catalog subscriptions** (4.5.6).
- Authentication: SSO (IAM Identity Center) or IAM credentials with the domain URL ✓.

## 7. Worked scenarios
1. *Glue job in private subnet, no internet, cheapest S3 access* → **S3 gateway endpoint**.
2. *Lambda in VPC with no NAT writes to Kinesis* → **interface VPC endpoint** for Kinesis.
3. *Only company buckets reachable through the S3 endpoint* → **VPC endpoint policy**.
4. *DB password rotates every 30 days, no job changes* → **Secrets Manager rotation** + Glue connection referencing the secret.
5. *Partner allowlists one IP* → **NAT gateway + EIP**.
6. *Hundreds of project prefixes, one policy* → ABAC (see 4.2).

## 8. Keyword → answer and traps
| Keyword | Answer | Trap |
|---|---|---|
| S3/DynamoDB private path, free | gateway endpoint | interface endpoint / NAT |
| Kinesis/Glue/KMS private path | interface endpoint | gateway |
| automatic credential rotation | Secrets Manager | Parameter Store |
| service assumes role | trust policy for service principal | permissions policy only |
| give a service a role | `iam:PassRole` | attach policy to service |
| org-wide ceiling | SCP | permission boundary on each role |
| managed = least ops | RDS/Glue/Athena | EC2-hosted |

<!-- source: guide/D4-security-governance/4.2-authorization-lakeformation.md -->

# Task 4.2 — Apply authorization mechanisms (D4)
Tags: ✓ verified 2026-10-20 (link) · ~ established, not re-fetched. Skills 4.2.1–4.2.6.

## 1. Custom IAM policies (4.2.1, 4.2.6)
- Use **AWS managed policies** for quick starts (e.g., `AWSGlueServiceRole`), **customer managed** when they are too broad/narrow, inline only for 1:1 binding.
- Least privilege recipe: specific **actions**, specific **resource ARNs**, **conditions** (prefix, tag, source VPC/IP, MFA, TLS, Region), no `*:*`; start with Access Analyzer–generated policy from CloudTrail activity ~; validate with policy simulator/Access Analyzer checks ~.
- Evaluation logic: explicit **Deny** wins → organization SCPs → permission boundary → session policy → identity/resource allow. Same-account: identity OR resource policy allow suffices; **cross-account**: both sides must allow (unless role assumption) ✓.
- Common data-engineering policy shapes: S3 prefix-scoped Get/Put/List with `s3:prefix` condition; `kms:Decrypt/GenerateDataKey` on the specific key; `glue:GetTable/GetPartitions` on catalog/database/table ARNs; `iam:PassRole` limited with `iam:PassedToService`; `logs:*` on a log group.

## 2. Store application and database credentials (4.2.2)
| | Secrets Manager | SSM Parameter Store |
|---|---|---|
| Purpose | secrets with lifecycle | config + secrets |
| Rotation | **automatic** (managed or Lambda) ✓ | none built-in |
| Cost | per secret/month + API calls | Standard parameters free; Advanced paid ~ |
| Cross-account | resource policy | via sharing Advanced parameters (RAM) ~ |
| Encryption | KMS always | SecureString (KMS) optional |
| Size | up to 64 KB ~ | 4 KB std / 8 KB adv ~ |
Pick: rotation or DB credentials → Secrets Manager; many config values + a few static secrets at lowest cost → Parameter Store SecureString ✓ (mock Q37). Never hard-code or put in env vars/plaintext S3.

## 3. Database users, groups, roles (4.2.3) — Redshift emphasis
- Redshift: database users/groups/**roles** (RBAC) with `GRANT … TO ROLE`, schema `USAGE`, table `SELECT`, **column-level GRANT**, **row-level security** policies, **dynamic data masking** by role, `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES`; authenticate with IAM (temporary credentials, `GetClusterCredentials`), IAM Identity Center/federation ~; `COPY/UNLOAD/Spectrum` use IAM roles attached to the cluster/namespace; **data sharing** permissions (4.5.1).
```sql
CREATE ROLE analyst;
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA sales TO ROLE analyst;
GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA sales TO ROLE analyst;
GRANT ROLE analyst TO "alice";
```
- RDS/Aurora: IAM database authentication, DB roles/grants, Secrets Manager rotation; DynamoDB: IAM fine-grained access (`dynamodb:LeadingKeys`, `dynamodb:Attributes` conditions ~).

## 4. Lake Formation (4.2.4) ✓ [LF hybrid access](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/hybrid-access-mode.html)
**What it is**: central, fine-grained access control over **Glue Data Catalog** resources and the S3 data behind them, for Athena, Redshift (Spectrum), EMR, Glue (named in 4.2.4 ✓).
- **Model**: register S3 location (role) → grant permissions on catalog objects to principals (IAM users/roles, SAML/IdC users, accounts, orgs): `SELECT, INSERT, DELETE, DESCRIBE, ALTER, DROP, CREATE_TABLE…`, column lists, **data filters** (row-level via filter expression, column-level inclusion/exclusion, **cell-level** = both). Effective access = **LF permission AND the IAM permission** for the calling service (opted-in principals need both ✓).
- **Credential vending**: LF issues scoped temporary credentials to integrated engines for registered locations; June 2026: table grants (SELECT=read, SUPER=read/write) can also govern *direct S3 file access* with EMR 7.13+ (non-English What's New text only [UNVERIFIED]).
- **IAMAllowedPrincipals**: virtual group that, when granted `Super`, makes a resource a plain **AWS Glue resource** — IAM only, LF *not* enforced ✓. To enforce LF, revoke it.
- **Hybrid access mode** ✓: two pathways to the *same* catalog objects — principals you **opt in** use LF permissions (and IAM), all others keep using IAM S3/Glue policies. Registering the S3 location in hybrid mode enforces only CREATE_TABLE, CREATE_PARTITION, UPDATE_TABLE by default. Use to adopt LF gradually without breaking existing jobs; for cross-account, set **cross-account version setting to 4** ✓; to convert an LF resource to hybrid, first opt in current principals and grant `Super` to IAMAllowedPrincipals ✓.
- **LF-tags (LF-TBAC)**: define tags (`domain=finance`, `sensitivity=pii`), attach to databases/tables/columns, grant permissions on tag expressions; scales to thousands of resources; satisfies *tag-based/attribute-based* (4.2.5).
- **Cross-account**: grant to external account/org; recipient admin re-grants to principals; tables appear via **resource links** (shared resource names) created in the recipient catalog; AWS RAM invitations underneath; S3 data in encrypted buckets also needs KMS key policy for the consumer.
- **Governed tables** (older LF feature) no longer in guide → use Iceberg/S3 Tables with LF/IAM. Limitation example ✓: Glue jobs on tables with *cell-level filters* can't use job bookmarks, push-down predicates, or `enableUpdateCatalog`.
- LF vs IAM/S3 policies: IAM/bucket policies = object-level, hard to scale to many tables/columns; LF = table/column/row/cell, central, audited in CloudTrail.

## 5. Authorization methods (4.2.5)
| Method | How | Use |
|---|---|---|
| **RBAC** | permissions bundled in roles/groups (IAM roles, Redshift roles, LF grants to roles) | stable job functions |
| **Policy-based** | explicit allow/deny statements on resources | baseline |
| **Tag-based / ABAC** | `aws:PrincipalTag/team` equals `aws:ResourceTag/team` (IAM) or LF-tags | scalable per-team/project access without per-team policies ✓ (topic mock Q62) |
| Resource-based | bucket/KMS/SQS/Lambda/catalog policies | cross-account, service-to-service |
Pick: many teams × many resources → ABAC/LF-tags; few stable roles → RBAC.

## 6. Least privilege checklist (4.2.6)
Scoped resources, separate roles per pipeline stage (ingest read-only raw; transform write curated), conditions for prefix/VPC/TLS, no wildcard principals in resource policies without conditions (KMS ✓ warning), remove unused permissions (Access Analyzer unused-access findings ~), rotate/avoid long-term keys, MFA for humans, break-glass roles audited.

## 7. Worked scenarios
1. *Analysts see all columns except `ssn` in Athena; central, auditable, least overhead* → **Lake Formation** column grant (not bucket policy/IAM deny).
2. *Existing jobs use IAM only; adopt LF gradually* → **hybrid access mode** ✓.
3. *Hundreds of project prefixes; one policy* → **ABAC** (principal tag = resource tag).
4. *Share lake tables with another account* → LF cross-account grant + resource link (+ KMS key policy).
5. *Support agents see last 4 card digits; finance sees full* → Redshift **dynamic data masking**.

## 8. Keyword → answer and traps
| Keyword | Answer | Trap |
|---|---|---|
| column/row/cell security on lake | Lake Formation (filters) | S3 policy |
| scalable permissions by attribute | LF-tags / ABAC | per-resource grants |
| migrate to LF gradually | hybrid access mode | delete IAM policies |
| LF not enforced | IAMAllowedPrincipals has Super | missing grant |
| rotation of DB secret | Secrets Manager | Parameter Store |
| cross-account needs | allow on both sides | one-sided policy |
| `AccessDenied` from KMS | key policy/IAM kms permissions | S3 bucket policy |

<!-- source: guide/D4-security-governance/4.3-encryption-masking.md -->

# Task 4.3 — Ensure data encryption and masking (D4)
Tags: ✓ verified 2026-10-20 (link) · ~ established, not re-fetched. Skills 4.3.1–4.3.4.

## 1. KMS essentials (4.3.2)
- **Key types**: AWS owned (invisible, service-managed), **AWS managed** (`aws/s3`, `aws/glue`…; created per service; policy not editable; **rotated every year automatically**, cannot be toggled ✓; cannot be used by other accounts ~ (standard rule)), **customer managed (CMK)** (you control policy, rotation, grants, aliases, deletion).
- **Key policy** is the root of trust for a KMS key; IAM policies work only if the key policy allows IAM (default statement enabling IAM) ✓. **Grants** = temporary, scoped delegation (used by AWS services such as EBS/RDS/Redshift). Use **aliases** to swap keys behind a name.
- **Envelope encryption**: `GenerateDataKey` → plaintext data key encrypts data locally, encrypted data key stored with the data; KMS `Encrypt` direct limit 4 KB ~. Services do this automatically.
- **Rotation** ✓ [KMS rotation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/rotate-keys.html): automatic rotation is optional for customer managed keys, only for **symmetric encryption keys with AWS_KMS-origin material**; default every **365 days**, custom **rotation period configurable** (and constrainable with `kms:RotationPeriodInDays`); **on-demand rotation** also available (also for imported-material symmetric keys); asymmetric, HMAC and custom-key-store keys need **manual rotation** (new key + alias swap). Key ID, ARN, aliases and policies **stay the same**; old key material is **retained** so old ciphertext still decrypts; rotation doesn't re-encrypt data or rotate data keys; billed for first and second rotation only; events in CloudTrail (`RotateKey`) and EventBridge ✓.
- **Multi-Region keys**: same key material in several Regions (DR, global tables, cross-Region replication) ~. **Imported key material** (BYOK), **custom key store** (CloudHSM) ~.
- Quotas: KMS API request rates are shared per account/Region — high-volume SSE-KMS workloads can throttle → use **S3 Bucket Keys** ✓ (fewer KMS calls) or data-key caching ~.

## 2. Encryption across account boundaries (4.3.3) ✓ [KMS external accounts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/key-policy-modifying-external-accounts.html)
Cross-account use needs **two permissions**: (1) the **key policy** (key account) allows the external account or specific principals; (2) an **IAM policy in the external account** delegates it. "The key policy determines who *can*; the IAM policy determines who *does*. Neither alone is sufficient" ✓. Cross-account permission applies only to crypto operations (Encrypt, Decrypt, ReEncrypt*, GenerateDataKey*), CreateGrant, DescribeKey, GetKeyRotationStatus, GetPublicKey, ListGrants, RetireGrant, RevokeGrant ✓ — other actions have no cross-account effect. Never `Principal: *` without conditions ✓. Cross-account calls are logged in both accounts' CloudTrail ✓. Use CMKs (AWS managed keys can't be shared).
```json
{"Sid":"AllowExternalAccount","Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::444455556666:root"},
 "Action":["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt","kms:ReEncrypt*","kms:GenerateDataKey*","kms:DescribeKey"],"Resource":"*"}
```
Patterns: cross-account S3 SSE-KMS read (bucket policy/role + key policy + IAM kms:Decrypt) ✓ mock Q4; S3 CRR with SSE-KMS (replication role needs kms on source and destination keys; destination key set in config) ~; encrypted Redshift/RDS snapshot sharing/copy (share the CMK; cross-Region Redshift needs **snapshot copy grant** in destination Region) ~; Lake Formation shared tables on encrypted buckets need key access for consumers.

## 3. Encryption at rest by service
| Service | At rest |
|---|---|
| S3 | SSE-S3 default for new objects ~; **SSE-KMS** (audit, key control; Bucket Keys ✓); **DSSE-KMS** ~; **SSE-C** (client supplies key each request); client-side |
| Redshift | cluster encrypted with KMS (or HSM); enabling later via snapshot restore/migration; snapshots inherit |
| RDS/Aurora | at creation (KMS); snapshot copy to encrypt an unencrypted DB |
| DynamoDB | always encrypted: owned (default), AWS managed, or CMK |
| Kinesis Data Streams | SSE-KMS (rotation limits: 25 key changes/24 h ✓) |
| Firehose | CMK for up to 500 streams ✓; encrypts delivery to S3 via destination settings |
| Glue | **security configuration** (S3 output, CloudWatch Logs, job bookmarks) + Data Catalog encryption ✓ |
| EMR | security configuration (at-rest: S3 EMRFS, local disk/EBS; in-transit: TLS) |
| MSK | KMS at rest; TLS in transit |
| SQS/SNS | SSE-KMS |
| Athena | encrypt query results (workgroup-enforced SSE-S3/KMS/CSE-KMS) ~ |
| CloudTrail Lake | encrypted by default; optional own KMS key (cannot be removed or changed once set ✓) |
| Secrets Manager | KMS |

## 4. Encryption in transit or before transit (4.3.4)
- **In transit**: TLS/HTTPS to all AWS APIs; enforce on S3 with bucket policy `aws:SecureTransport = false` → Deny ✓; Redshift `require_ssl` and **TLS ≥ 1.2 enforced from 2026-10-31** ✓; RDS `rds.force_ssl` ~; MSK client TLS; Kinesis/Firehose HTTPS; VPC endpoints keep traffic off the internet; VPN/Direct Connect + MACsec ~; EMR in-transit via security configuration.
- **Before transit (client-side)**: encrypt data before sending — AWS Encryption SDK / S3 Encryption Client / KMS `GenerateDataKey` — when no service (or AWS) should see plaintext ✓ (mock Q64). DynamoDB Encryption Client ~.

## 5. Masking and anonymisation (4.3.1)
| Technique | Where |
|---|---|
| Static masking/redaction/hashing in ETL | **Glue sensitive data detection** transform (detect + mask/hash), DataBrew (mask, hash, substitute, shuffle), Spark UDFs, Lambda |
| Dynamic masking at query time | **Redshift dynamic data masking** (policy by role), LF data filters/column exclusion, Quick column-level security |
| Row/column restriction | Lake Formation filters, Redshift RLS, Quick RLS |
| Tokenisation/pseudonymisation | Lambda + KMS/HMAC, deterministic hashing for joinability |
| Anonymisation/k-anonymity/generalisation | aggregation, bucketing, noise (differential privacy ~), suppression |
| Discovery | **Macie** (S3), Glue sensitive data detection, catalog tags |
Compliance logic: mask **before** analytics zones for GDPR/HIPAA/PCI; keep re-identification keys separate; log access.

## 6. Worked scenarios
1. *High-volume SSE-KMS bucket throttles KMS and costs rise* → **S3 Bucket Keys** ✓.
2. *Account B role can't read account A SSE-KMS objects* → add key-policy statement (A) + IAM `kms:Decrypt` (B) ✓.
3. *CMK must rotate yearly with unchanged ID/alias* → enable **automatic rotation** ✓.
4. *Encrypted Redshift snapshots to another Region* → **snapshot copy grant** + destination KMS key.
5. *Support agents see last-4 card digits* → **Redshift dynamic data masking**.
6. *Regulation: AWS must never see plaintext* → **client-side encryption** before upload.

## 7. Keyword → answer and traps
| Keyword | Answer | Trap |
|---|---|---|
| rotate key yearly, same ARN | automatic rotation (CMK) | create new key each year |
| AWS managed key cross-account | not possible → CMK | share aws/s3 |
| reduce KMS calls | Bucket Keys | more keys |
| enforce HTTPS | `aws:SecureTransport` deny | default encryption |
| encrypt before upload | client-side | SSE-S3 |
| mask by role at query time | DDM / LF filters | ETL copy |
| detect PII in S3 | Macie | GuardDuty |

<!-- source: guide/D4-security-governance/4.4-audit-logs.md -->

# Task 4.4 — Prepare logs for audit (D4)
Tags: ✓ verified 2026-10-20 (link) · ~ established, not re-fetched. Skills 4.4.1–4.4.5. Overlaps D3 3.3 (operations view).

## 1. Log sources → destinations (who/what/when)
| Evidence | Source | Store / analyse |
|---|---|---|
| API calls (control plane) | **CloudTrail** management events | S3 trail (+ Athena), CloudWatch Logs, **CloudTrail Lake** |
| Object/item-level data access | CloudTrail **data events** (S3 object ops, Lambda invoke, DynamoDB items) — opt-in ✓ | same |
| Unusual API activity | CloudTrail **Insights** | EventBridge/SNS |
| Application/job logs | **CloudWatch Logs** | Logs Insights, subscription → Firehose/OpenSearch/S3 → Athena |
| Config changes/compliance | **AWS Config** | S3 snapshots, rules, conformance packs |
| S3 access | server access logs, CloudTrail data events | S3 → Athena |
| Network | VPC Flow Logs, Route 53 resolver logs | S3/CloudWatch → Athena |
| DB activity | Redshift audit logs (connection/user/user-activity), RDS/Aurora logs (audit/slow query/error), DynamoDB via CloudTrail | S3/CloudWatch |
| Query activity | Athena query history/CloudTrail, Lake Formation access in CloudTrail | |
| Large-scale cluster logs | EMR log URI → S3; Spark/Hive logs | EMR/Glue Spark, Athena |

## 2. CloudTrail (4.4.1)
- **Event types**: management (default; control-plane such as `CreateJob`, `PutBucketPolicy`, `DisableKey`), **data** (high-volume object-level; must be enabled per trail/data store), **Insights**, network activity ✓ (Lake lists management, data, network activity events), plus Config items, Audit Manager evidence, and non-AWS events in Lake ✓.
- **Trails**: multi-Region, organization trails; deliver to S3 (+ SNS notifications, CloudWatch Logs); **log file integrity validation** (digest files); encrypt with KMS; event history (90 d) ~.
- Real-time alerts: EventBridge rule on CloudTrail API events (e.g., `kms.amazonaws.com` `DisableKey`/`ScheduleKeyDeletion`) → SNS ✓ (mock Q65). Cross-account KMS calls logged in both accounts ✓.

## 3. CloudTrail Lake (4.4.3) ✓ [CloudTrail Lake](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-lake.html)
- **SQL queries on events** (Trino `SELECT` syntax) over **event data stores** — immutable collections of events (converted to **Apache ORC**) selected by advanced event selectors; one event category per store; **organization event data stores** across Regions/accounts; join across stores; saved queries; dashboards (managed, custom ≤10 widgets, highlights); query results kept 7 days and can be saved to S3; natural-language query generator.
- **Retention** ✓: up to **3,653 days (~10 y)** with the one-year-extendable pricing option or **2,557 days (~7 y)** with the seven-year option; pricing = ingestion + storage + **data scanned per query**; optional own KMS key (cannot be removed or changed afterwards).
- **Federate** an event data store to the Glue Data Catalog and query it from **Athena** ✓; cross-account access with resource-based policy ✓; integrations ingest non-AWS activity via `PutAuditEvents`.
- ⚠ **Availability change** ✓: CloudTrail Lake is **not open to new customers starting 2026-05-31**; existing customers continue. The exam guide v1.1 still lists skill 4.4.3 — know the concept; for new accounts the alternative is trails to S3 + Athena. [exam relevance of the change: unknown]
- Lake vs trail+Athena: Lake = managed, no setup of tables, org-wide SQL, retention features, higher per-scan cost; S3 trail + Athena = cheapest storage, DIY partitioning/projection.

## 4. CloudWatch Logs for application logs (4.4.2) ✓ [Logs Insights](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/AnalyzingLogData.html)
Log groups/streams, retention policies (default never expire → set it), KMS encryption, metric filters, subscription filters (to Kinesis/Firehose/Lambda/OpenSearch), export tasks to S3, cross-account/Region log centralisation (monitoring account ✓), data protection policies to detect/mask sensitive data in logs ~, log classes (Standard/Infrequent Access) ~. Glue **continuous logging** and Spark UI logs ✓; Lambda automatically logs to CloudWatch with the execution role's logs permissions.

## 5. Analyse logs with AWS services (4.4.4)
| Need | Service |
|---|---|
| Ad hoc on recent logs, seconds–minutes | **CloudWatch Logs Insights** (Logs Insights QL, OpenSearch PPL, OpenSearch SQL ✓; 100 concurrent QL queries/account; 60-min timeout; results kept 7 d; billed per GB scanned ✓; field indexes cut scan) |
| SQL over archived logs in S3 (CloudTrail, ALB, VPC Flow, S3 access) | **Athena** (partition projection for date-partitioned logs) |
| Near-real-time search, correlation, dashboards, alerting | **OpenSearch Service** (ingest via Firehose/subscription filter/OpenSearch Ingestion) |
| Managed SQL across org events | CloudTrail Lake |
| Dashboards | Managed Grafana, Quick |

## 6. Integrating services for logging at volume (4.4.5)
Large volume pipelines: sources → **Firehose** (buffer/compress/convert to Parquet, partition by date via dynamic partitioning) → **S3** → **Glue/EMR** Spark for parsing/enrichment/aggregation → **Athena/Redshift** for audit queries; or → OpenSearch for search. **EMR** when petabyte-scale/custom parsing (Spark, Hive) of "big data application logs" ✓ (skills 3.3.8, 4.4.5). Use compression, columnar conversion, partitions (`year/month/day/hour`), lifecycle to Glacier for retention, Object Lock for tamper resistance ~.

## 7. Worked scenarios
1. *Who deleted objects from the bucket?* → CloudTrail **S3 data events** (write) ✓.
2. *Immediate alert when a KMS key is disabled* → EventBridge on CloudTrail events → SNS.
3. *Org-wide SQL on events without infrastructure* → **CloudTrail Lake** (existing customers) / trail + Athena.
4. *Low-cost ad hoc SQL on CloudTrail logs in S3* → **Athena table with partition projection**.
5. *50 TB/day raw app logs parsed for audit reports* → **Spark on EMR/Glue** from S3.
6. *Searchable logs in seconds* → CloudWatch Logs → Firehose → **OpenSearch**.

## 8. Keyword → answer and traps
| Keyword | Answer | Trap |
|---|---|---|
| object-level API audit | S3 data events | management events |
| SQL on events, managed | CloudTrail Lake | CloudWatch metrics |
| tamper-evident trail | log file validation | Config |
| long-term cheap log SQL | S3 + Athena | Logs Insights |
| near-real-time search | OpenSearch | Athena |
| huge raw logs parse | EMR / Glue Spark | Lambda |

# Task 4.5 — Understand data privacy and governance (D4)
Tags: ✓ verified 2026-10-20 (link) · ~ established, not re-fetched · (S) secondary source only. Skills 4.5.1–4.5.7 (4.5.6/4.5.7 NEW in v1.1).

## 1. Permissions for data sharing (4.5.1)
| Pattern | When | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| **Redshift data sharing** ✓ | share live warehouse data across clusters/workgroups/accounts/Regions without copying; reads and now writes | producer `CREATE DATASHARE` + `GRANT USAGE … TO ACCOUNT/NAMESPACE`; consumer `CREATE DATABASE … FROM DATASHARE`; cross-account needs authorize/associate; transactional consistency ✓ |
| **Lake Formation cross-account** | share catalog tables/columns/rows | grant to account/org, resource links (RAM) |
| **S3 bucket policy / Access Points** | object-level sharing | resource policies, Access Points, presigned URLs (temporary) ~ |
| **SageMaker Catalog subscription** | governed business sharing | publish → subscribe → owner approves → grants provisioned ✓(S) |
| **AWS Data Exchange** | commercial third-party datasets | subscribe/publish; also Redshift datashares can be licensed ✓ |
| **Clean rooms** | joint analysis without exposing raw data | AWS Clean Rooms ~ (not in the guide's list) |
Principle: share the minimum (columns/rows), prefer live shares over copies, log with CloudTrail, encrypt (shared KMS CMK), revoke centrally.

## 2. PII identification (4.5.2) ✓ [Macie](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/macie/latest/user/what-is-macie.html)
- **Macie** = ML + pattern matching to find sensitive data **in Amazon S3 only**; (1) **automated sensitive data discovery** (continuous sampling across the S3 estate) and (2) **discovery jobs** (targeted, one-time or recurring); **managed data identifiers** (PII, financial, credentials; many countries) + **custom data identifiers** (regex + keywords + proximity) + **allow lists**; also an S3 **bucket inventory** with posture checks (public access, sharing, encryption) → **policy findings**; **sensitive data findings** with severity; findings → **EventBridge** and **Security Hub (CSPM)** ✓; multi-account via Organizations delegated admin; 30-day free trial; **does not mask or modify data**.
- Combine with **Lake Formation**: classify, then tag columns with LF-tags (e.g., `pii=true`) and restrict analyst grants to non-PII tag values ✓ (mock Q26). Remediate through EventBridge → Lambda (tag, quarantine, notify).
- Others: **Glue sensitive data detection** (in ETL; detect/mask/hash), **DataBrew**, CloudWatch Logs data protection ~, Comprehend PII ~, Redshift/Aurora not scanned by Macie.

## 3. Preventing backups/replication to disallowed Regions (4.5.3)
- **SCP** denying actions when `aws:RequestedRegion` ∉ approved list (with exemptions for global services) ✓ preventive; **S3 CRR rules** only to approved Regions; **AWS Backup** plans/copy rules limited to approved Regions; snapshot copy, DynamoDB global tables and Aurora Global DB replicas only in approved Regions; KMS multi-Region keys avoided/limited; Config rules + Access Analyzer + CloudTrail to *detect*; Control Tower region deny guardrail ~; S3 Block Public Access; Organizations tag/backup policies ~.
- Detective vs preventive: SCP = prevent (preferred); Config/CloudTrail = detect/alert.

## 4. AWS Config (4.5.4)
Records **resource configuration history** and evaluates **rules** (managed/custom) → compliance; **conformance packs**, aggregators (multi-account/Region), remediation via Systems Manager Automation (e.g., enforce S3 default encryption) ✓ mock Q37, timeline of changes ("viewing configuration changes" ✓ v1.1 wording); Config items can feed CloudTrail Lake ✓. Not for API-call audit (CloudTrail) or PII (Macie).

## 5. Data sovereignty (4.5.5)
Data subject to the laws of the country where it is stored/processed: control **where data lives and who can access it** — Region selection, SCP region guardrails, single-Region KMS keys (and who holds them), restricted replication/backup, in-Region processing (Glue/EMR/Athena in the same Region), network controls (PrivateLink, no internet egress), access controls with LF/IAM, audit evidence (CloudTrail/Config), AWS European Sovereign Cloud (new Region family; Glue 5.1 available there Aug 2026 ✓), Local Zones/Outposts for local residency ~. Combine **residency** (location) + **sovereignty** (jurisdiction/control) + **privacy** (PII handling).

## 6. SageMaker Catalog and projects (4.5.6) (S)
Producers publish assets/data products into the catalog from their **project**; consumers (other projects) **search, request access (subscribe)**; the owner/approver approves; for managed assets (Glue tables under Lake Formation, Redshift tables) the catalog **creates the grants** automatically; access is then exercised inside the consumer **project** through its project role; all actions auditable; supports business glossary & metadata forms; in IAM-based domains custom asset types allowed (2026). Compare with Glue Data Catalog (technical metadata, no subscription workflow) and Lake Formation (enforcement engine underneath).
Decision: "approval workflow + business metadata + cross-team discovery" → SageMaker Catalog; "enforce column/row permissions" → Lake Formation; "who changed config" → Config.

## 7. Governance framework and sharing patterns (4.5.7)
**Framework pillars**: ownership & stewardship (data owners, stewards, domains/data mesh); classification & tagging (sensitivity, PII; LF-tags, glossary); policy & access (least privilege, ABAC, approvals); quality & lineage (DQ rules, lineage, SLAs); lifecycle & retention (S3 lifecycle, TTL, legal hold); security (encryption, key mgmt, network); audit & compliance (CloudTrail, Config, Macie, reports); cost accountability (tags, Budgets).
**Organisational patterns**: *centralised* (one team governs; Lake Formation admin), *federated/data mesh* (domain teams own data products; central guardrails; SageMaker Unified Studio domains/domain units/projects ✓(S)), *hub-and-spoke* (central catalog + account-per-domain, cross-account LF sharing). **Sharing patterns**: live share (Redshift datashare), catalog-mediated subscription, cross-account LF grants, S3 Access Points, replication (CRR for DR only), marketplace (Data Exchange), copy-with-masking for external parties.

## 8. Backup, DR, residency checklist (links to 2.3.6)
AWS Backup (cross-Region/account, vault lock), snapshot sharing with CMKs, restore tests, RPO/RTO tiers; ensure DR Region respects sovereignty.

## 9. Worked scenarios
1. *Find PII in S3 then hide PII columns from analysts in Athena* → **Macie** + **LF-tags** column grants ✓.
2. *Another account must query warehouse tables live* → **Redshift data sharing**.
3. *EU data and its DR copy must stay in EU* → **SCP region deny** + CRR/backup only to EU Regions + Region-scoped KMS ✓ (mock Q43/Q69).
4. *Detect and auto-fix unencrypted buckets* → **Config rule + remediation**.
5. *Consumer project requests asset; owner approves; access provisioned* → **SageMaker Catalog subscription**.

## 10. Keyword → answer and traps
| Keyword | Answer | Trap |
|---|---|---|
| discover PII in S3 | Macie | GuardDuty / Config |
| mask PII automatically | Glue sensitive data detection / DDM | Macie |
| share live warehouse data | Redshift data sharing | UNLOAD |
| prevent other Regions | SCP aws:RequestedRegion | Config (detective) |
| configuration drift/history | Config | CloudTrail |
| business glossary + approvals | SageMaker Catalog | Glue catalog |
| decentralised ownership | data mesh / domains | single admin |
